text:
Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have called NFL games together since 2002. Six Super Bowls, two networks, more than 20 years in the same booth. And right now, fans watching Monday Night Football say you can feel that something is off between them.

There's a reason. Back in May, Buck quietly agreed to a six-year, $108 million extension with ESPN that runs through the 2030 season. Aikman's five-year, $90 million deal ends after ESPN's Super Bowl broadcast on February 14, 2027. As of last month, ESPN reportedly hadn't offered him a formal extension.

According to Puck, Aikman felt "double-crossed" when he found out. Then The Athletic reported the two got into it off the air before the Bills-Rams game on October 12. Buck reportedly started with, "You are not going to f---ing talk to me?" and later told him, "I'm not the reason you don't have a contract." Aikman's reported answer: "I just never thought you'd do it to me."

Buck has said they always handled their contracts separately and never planned to sign together. Charles Barkley took Buck's side: "It's not Joe Buck's job to get him a deal." Aikman says there's "a time and a place" to talk about it, and that he'll finish the season and become a free agent. CBS, Amazon and Netflix have all come up as possible landing spots.

Barkley's right, it isn't Buck's job. But after 20-plus years next to somebody, you'd at least expect a heads-up before he locks in $108 million and leaves you on a deal with an end date. Aikman doesn't need ESPN's sympathy, though. He needs the open market, and a free agent who has called six Super Bowls is going to get paid by somebody.

text:
Why Steve Jobs Is ISFP

Fi is introverted unit judgment, centered on reading and evaluating the agent's own state. When Fi has high decision authority, the person places great weight on personal feelings, aesthetics, and internal preferences, using them as major criteria for evaluating things.
The most striking manifestation of Fi in Jobs is the exceptionally high decision authority of his personal aesthetic standards.
During product development, even when a design met technical requirements and had consumed substantial resources, Jobs might demand changes if he felt it was not beautiful enough, lacked harmony, or failed to produce the desired user experience. His long collaboration with Apple's chief designer Jony Ive strongly illustrates this pattern.
An especially persuasive example comes from the development of the early Macintosh.
Jobs wanted not only an attractive exterior but also aesthetically pleasing circuit boards hidden within the enclosure. When he found certain chip arrangements visually unsatisfactory, he asked the engineers to rearrange them.
The engineers were puzzled: consumers would never see the circuit board inside the case, so why should its appearance matter if it worked properly?
Yet Jobs insisted that even unseen parts should be as beautiful as possible. He offered the example of a cabinetmaker: a truly good craftsman would not use poor-quality wood on the back of a cabinet merely because it faced the wall and was invisible to others.
This episode particularly reveals the characteristics of Fi.
If aesthetics were only a way of winning consumer approval, there would be no need to make hidden circuit boards more attractive. Jobs's aesthetic standards did not depend entirely on external evaluation. Even without an audience, he wanted products to meet his own internal standards.
For him, aesthetics was not merely a commercial instrument, but a subjective judgment with intrinsic value.
Jobs's decision to audit calligraphy classes at Reed College when young similarly illustrates Fi as the first driving force.
In his later Stanford commencement address, he recalled that he did not study calligraphy because he foresaw its future usefulness in computers, but because typefaces, spacing, and typography fascinated him. He voluntarily immersed himself in them simply because they provided aesthetic satisfaction.
Only years later did these experiences find their way into Macintosh typography.
Jobs's cognitive motivation began in his own aesthetic experience. Personal feelings drove voluntary exploration, which only later generated practical value.
Se is extraverted complexity compression, centered on selecting and processing what matters in present reality and continually adjusting cognition and action through direct participation and immediate feedback.
Jobs's Se was especially evident in his aesthetic perception of real products and his direct involvement with them.
He was exceptionally sensitive to typography, colors, lines, housing curvature, material textures, button placement, and user interaction. These were not merely abstract design concepts but actual objects whose qualities could only be fully grasped through seeing, touching, and using them.
Numerous details attest to this hands-on involvement. In choosing materials, Jobs insisted on precisely machined real metal and glass rather than surface coatings that merely imitated their textures. To achieve the desired result, he was willing to invest in new manufacturing techniques and facilities. He persistently sought extreme thinness in product design, making the dimensions of the iPhone, MacBook, and iPad major objects of attention; in pursuit of a slimmer iPhone, Apple even adopted a sealed design in which users could not directly replace the battery. Together with Ive, he repeatedly studied the shape of product boxes, internal trays, opening mechanisms, and tactile qualities, treating unboxing itself as a carefully designed experience. From the iPod to the iPhone, packaging became not merely a protective container but a component refined almost as an artwork. Even the shape of MacBook power adapters, the feel of magnetic connectors snapping into place, and the curvature of the iPad's edges received his attention. Together these cases show that Jobs was not content simply to state abstract aesthetic requirements; he continually examined the materials, forms, dimensions, and sensory properties of particular objects, refining products through real-world feedback.
During product development, Jobs habitually participated directly in design reviews, required engineers and designers to present physical prototypes, and personally examined, experienced, and commented on them.
A product that appears reasonable in concept may not feel satisfactory in reality. Actual material texture, button response, screen appearance, and the overall impression produced by assembled parts must be evaluated through direct experience.
Jobs's sustained attention to these details illustrates Se's deep involvement with reality.
Fi and Se worked together in a distinctive way: Fi determined what kind of product was worth creating, while Se converted that aesthetic standard into a concrete object through direct perception and repeated adjustments.
This also explains Jobs's distinctive manner of execution.
He was not content merely to establish strategy, allocate resources, and wait for management to finish the work. He preferred entering the process of product creation directly and organizing design, engineering, and management around concrete products.
From the Macintosh to the iPod and then the iPhone, this strongly product-centered approach remained remarkably consistent.
Jobs also displayed noteworthy Ni tendencies.
Ni is introverted complexity compression, integrating complex information into relatively stable overall pictures. Unlike Se's emphasis on what matters in present reality, Ni focuses more on consolidating internal models and establishing long-term direction.
When Jobs returned to Apple in 1997, he dramatically simplified the product lineup, concentrating previously scattered activities into a few core product directions.
This was not merely an adjustment of business efficiency. It can also be understood in Ni terms: faced with complicated products and business structures, he favored forming a highly unified overall conception and deciding from it which directions to retain or discard.
Such integration of long-term direction belongs to a different level of cognition from the Se he displayed in particular products.
Nevertheless, simplification of product lines alone cannot prove Ni. It is more suitable as supplementary evidence for participation by the third function in overall planning.
Overall, Jobs's most stable cognitive structure began with personal aesthetics and subjective experience as important first driving forces, and translated internal standards into actual products through intensive practical involvement.
In this analysis, Fi determines value and aesthetic standards, Se supports practical perception and concrete creation, and Ni participates in the integration of long-term product direction.
A Fi-dominant, Se-auxiliary cognitive structure is the principal basis for classifying Jobs as ISFP.

Gold Movie

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
This reminds me of a situation I encountered in MN when I was 18, back in 2004. I had to wait until I was 18 to get my license and I answered an ad about a 1994 Ford Taurus for sale for $200, quite a distance away. I want to say he lived in Buffalo but I can’t fully remember nor do I remember his name but I believe he was Russian. My parents dropped me off at his house to buy the car and left me to handle the transaction myself. 

I got the car and didn’t know anything about insurance etc. back then and never got the title. I remember I had to stay in contact with him because he couldn’t fully do the sale or something right there on the spot but told me I could drive away with it since I was so excited to have my first car of my own. I do remember him asking me for my ID though and it was just really weird looking back on it. I went to buy it but instead I ended up sort of renting it from him for the $200 as I was never able to get it fully into my name. It was after I enlisted in the Marine Corps and was waiting to go to basic training. 

It was the very first car I ever tried to buy and had no one to help me so I drove it and the guy maintained contact with me. I only needed it for about 3-4 months before leaving for basic and ended up sort of renting it from him. I assumed he had insurance on it and ended up getting 2 no insurance tickets in it, one of which was when I was going to get rid of the car after finding out there was no insirance. Since it wasn’t mine, I didn’t think I could get insurance on it. I remember bits and fragments but he wanted to be like my “sugar daddy” or something. 

I brought a “friend” with me one time I met him because I felt something was off. He paid for us to go out to eat once and eventually after getting a ticket, I told him I no longer wanted the car. He tried to get my friend to buy it next and the last time I saw him he offered to pay me $3000 to marry his nephew for a green card! I told him no way, I’m going into the Marine Corps. I would never do that because it’s wrong and I surely wouldn’t jeopardize my career before it even began. This man was significantly older maybe 40-50 years. 

Well, when I tried to get rid of it, the gas pedal stuck, I got pulled over and another no insurance ticket on my record 2-3 weeks later. The car was cursed! It was impounded and I did some further investigation on it because I found out it had a salvaged title. 

Out of curiosity and to make sense of the weirdness, I ended up finding out the name of the actual owner of the car from the state and got his phone number to call him. He told me he had no idea who the guy was who sold it to me or how he got ahold of it. He said it was salvaged and sent to a junk yard. Creepy shit! I could have ended up like one of those Epstein girls if I hadn’t had sense about me. 

I didn’t care how poor I was, I wasn’t going to take money to break the law and I didn’t need a “sugar daddy” at the expense of my morals and values. I had a job running the front desk at a hotel at that time with Marriot. $10/hr was good enough for me but I had just quit to spend time with my friends before leaving for basic. Money was tight, being that I was on my own at 18. Feel like I dodged a bullet there! 

Thank God for God 🙏❤️

text:
Comparative political theory

* John Rawls: Justice as fairness offers a framework for evaluating institutional inequalities, although Ambedkar's historical engagement with caste predates Rawls's mature theory.

* Iris Marion Young: Structural injustice and group-differentiated representation illuminate Ambedkar's concerns about political voice.

* Nancy Fraser: Redistribution, recognition and representation provide a contemporary framework for interpreting economic, cultural and political dimensions of caste injustice.

* Axel Honneth: Recognition theory explains why humiliation and denial of social respect are not reducible to income deprivation.

* Jürgen Habermas: Deliberative democracy illuminates the importance of reasoned dialogue, provided participants possess meaningful equality.

* Hannah Arendt: Political action and public participation help distinguish citizenship from passive legal membership.

* John Stuart Mill: Liberty and representative government offer comparative perspectives on minority protection and majority power.

* Rousseau: The tension between collective sovereignty and individual freedom raises questions about whether social unity can coexist with persistent inequality.

PSIR analytical proposition: Gandhi and Ambedkar expose a permanent democratic tension: collective solidarity is necessary for political community, but solidarity becomes oppressive when it requires subordinated groups to surrender autonomy.

Additional theoretical application: Rawls's fair equality of opportunity, Fraser's participatory parity and Young's structural injustice provide distinct lenses for evaluating whether constitutional equality produces meaningful social participation. These are comparative applications, not claims of direct historical influence.

Someone reached out to me offering $40 per post to promote their project We discussed the terms, and everything seemed straightforward at first.

The next step was to review a campaign document they shared through a link. Unfortunately, I couldn't access it on my phone, and my PC wasn't available at the time.

I later became uncomfortable with the idea of opening the link on my PC, especially after hearing about similar cases where people lost access to their accounts through this process 

I eventually came across a post exposing this exact project as a scam.

Thankfully, I didn't download anything or proceed with the offer

I'm sharing this because I know how many people in Web3 are constantly looking for opportunities, trying to get their first paid gig or secure collaborations. Unfortunately, scammers know this too, and they're willing to use those ambitions against people.

Please don't let the excitement of a paid opportunity make you overlook security red flags Always be careful with links and files sent by people approaching you with promotional deals.

The account involved is @Samanth8396031  Please report it if you have experienced or identified the same suspicious activity.

I'll leave screenshots of our conversation below.

Stay safe, everyone.

Shiʿism in medieval Muslim Spain (al-Andalus) was historically marginal, as the ruling Umayyad dynasty and subsequent local states maintained a strict adherence to Sunni Islam (specifically the Maliki school of jurisprudence) and viewed Shiʿism with political and religious hostility. 

Historical Context in al-Andalus (711–1492)
Umayyad Hostility: Al-Andalus was founded as a western continuation of the Umayyad regime, which possessed a deeply rooted anti-Alid heritage. Public or systematic Shiʿism was heavily suppressed or discouraged. 
Political vs. Religious Shiʿism: Apparent Shiʿi influences in al-Andalus were often political rather than theological. For example, post-Umayyad splinter entities like the Banu Hammud (Hammudid dynasty) claimed Alid lineage to assert political legitimacy and Caliphral authority rather than promoting Twelver or Ismaili religious doctrines. 
Intellectual and Literary Traces: Isolated figures—such as the poet Ibn Hani al-Andalusi—did embrace Ismaili Shiʿism before migrating to North Africa, and occasional intellectual or esoteric manuscripts hinted at Shiʿi traditions, though mainstream Andalusi society remained firmly Sunni. 
Diverse Early Currents: Chronicles and historical analyses note that early North African and Andalusi populations included various minor groups or factions with pro-Alid or sectarian leanings, though they were absorbed or marginalized over time. 

Modern Shia Islam in Spain
Demographics: Today, out of a total Muslim population of over 2.5 million in Spain, Shia Muslims number roughly 50,000. 
Communities and Origins: The modern Shia community is diverse, composed of expatriates and immigrants from Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, and Pakistan, alongside a growing number of native Spanish converts. 
Public Life and Practices: Shia cultural and religious associations operate community centers and imambargahs in major metropolitan areas like Madrid and Barcelona. These groups organize annual public and communal commemorations, such as Ashura during the Islamic month of Muharram.

text:
7/7 🏁 FINAL POST — BASALT v0.4.1 BENCHMARK CONCLUSIONS

This is the second and final additional post in our thread about testing the dense Qwen3.8-27B-QUASAR-NVFP4 model on an RTX 5090 Laptop with 24GB VRAM.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🐢 4. WHAT HAPPENS BEYOND VRAM CAPACITY?

At 256K, the entire KV cache no longer fits in GPU memory.

We used --kv-resident to move part of the KV cache into system RAM.

Results:

📦 Plain decoding — 4.7 tok/s

⚡ DFlash 2 — 5.1 tok/s

DFlash 2 acceleration dropped from 3.2× at 131K to just 1.09× at 256K.

The reason is the bandwidth limitation between system RAM and the GPU.

Our laptop supports PCIe 5.0 x16, but the actual negotiated connection runs at PCIe 4.0 x8 — 16 GT/s per lane.

Measured CPU→GPU bandwidth: 14.4 GB/s.

Once KV-cache transfers become the main bottleneck, speculative decoding offers almost no advantage.

This does not mean the model is incapable of processing 256K tokens.

It means the performance of this particular configuration is primarily limited by data transfer.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🧠 5. LONG-CONTEXT RETRIEVAL ACCURACY

We embedded five control records into long documents and attempted to retrieve them.

The initial instruction was:

“Find and list all control records.”

Result: 0/5.

However, we discovered a methodological issue in the follow-up request, so this result cannot be considered a reliable measurement of the model’s ability to independently identify every record.

We then performed targeted retrieval tests, asking for each control record by its exact identifier.

Results:

✅ 131K context — 5/5 correct.

✅ 256K context — 5/5 correct.

Even at 256K, with part of the KV cache residing in system RAM, the model correctly retrieved all five requested values.

This distinction is important.

Technically accepting a long context, retrieving a specific fact by a known identifier, and independently identifying all relevant facts are different capabilities.

We confirmed successful targeted retrieval, but we have not established reliable free-form discovery of every relevant fact.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📊 6. FINAL BENCHMARK RESULTS

On the RTX 5090 Laptop 24GB, running Basalt v0.4.1 with the dense Qwen3.8-27B-QUASAR-NVFP4 model:

🏆 Maximum generation speed on an individual task: 194.3 tok/s

⚡ Maximum speed during an individual response quarter: 264.3 tok/s

🚀 Standard chat: up to 121 tok/s

✅ Maximum fully GPU-resident context:

• Without DFlash — 203,776 positions
• With DFlash 2 — 140,288 positions

📦 With an actual input prompt of 197,886 tokens, plain decoding maintained 23.5 tok/s.

🐢 At 256K, with partial KV-cache offloading to RAM, generation speed dropped to approximately 5 tok/s.

Plain decoding remained remarkably stable throughout each continuous response.

DFlash 2 behaved differently: generation speed could vary significantly within a single response, sometimes increasing substantially after the first quarter.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 7. THE MAIN TAKEAWAY

The theoretical memory footprint of a KV cache is not the same as the maximum context an inference engine can actually allocate in VRAM.

And even a powerful GPU cannot guarantee high performance when data must constantly move across a relatively slow interconnect.

This is why benchmarking the entire system matters more than looking at isolated GPU specifications.

Real engine. Real model. Real hardware. Real workloads.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

https://t.co/ZYrBaYL3Os

Blazers @ Wolves
🏀 Deni and Donovan did well. The others did not. Wolves defense strikes again.

text:
3/10 THE FAA: ONE NEW ROUTER MEETS A NETWORK OF OLD ONES

What happened: the FAA stopped all departures nationwide. Roughly 3,500 planes already flying landed safely.

Why, according to the FAA: its legacy telecom network became unstable when data poured in at about 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds. The flood came from two remote sites, in Amarillo, Texas, and El Dorado, Arkansas, where contractor L3Harris had installed new routers.

How it spread: radar feeds and radio links at 17 of 22 en route centers became unreliable. Secretary Duffy says some of the receiving routers date to 2001.

Fix so far: the routers' broadcast function was disabled, including on about 60 similar units. The root cause is still being tested at L3Harris's lab in Florida.

The pattern piece: the trigger was routine work, part of replacing copper lines that were being retired. The weakest moment for any system is often the moment someone changes it.

What it means for you: when the FAA stops traffic, your airline's app is the fastest place to find your options, and DOT refund rules apply no matter why a flight was canceled (post 9).

Not confirmed: whether satellite backup links would have helped. Elon Musk says free Starlinks were offered and refused. DOT and the FAA haven't responded, and the FAA describes a network that was flooded, not cut.

5/10 WHERE THE INVESTIGATION STANDS (AS OF MONDAY NIGHT)

Confirmed:
• Both routers were removed from the Texas and Arkansas sites and are at L3Harris headquarters in Florida for "deep diagnostics testing." FAA, Juniper and Cisco engineers are assisting (Duffy, Sunday).
• An FAA team was at the lab Monday analyzing "the router that was the likely cause" (Duffy, Monday).
• The FBI offered to help. Duffy: "We think it was the installation or the router that was the bad actor," but investigators remain open to other findings.
• "No indication of a foreign cyberattack" (Duffy).

Unknown:
• The exact root cause: a defect in the device, its configuration, or how it was installed.
• Why a router at one remote site could destabilize 17 of 22 centers.
• Whether the FAA will publish a full report, and when. It hasn't given a date.

Questions the lab work should answer: was the broadcast setting on by default or set during installation, and why did the Amarillo unit, installed weeks earlier, only start flooding when El Dorado's came online?

In the meantime, the FAA has already switched off the broadcast feature on about 60 similar routers (post 7), so the immediate risk is being managed while the cause is found.

Also worth knowing: Fox News described it as the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.

text:
Perseverance confirms hydrated-silica-rich rocks at Idubi

Perseverance has confirmed that a cluster of light-coloured rocks at Idubi is rich in hydrated silica and does not consist of igneous rock, distinguishing the find from the kinds of stones the rover team had examined there before. The rocks are also brighter than the igneous and impactite material the team had investigated previously, and their pale appearance sets them apart from the darker, commonly dust-coated ground nearby. The update describes the rocks as large enough to provide a more promising investigation opportunity than the silica-rich material Perseverance encountered earlier on Jezero crater’s inner rim. It gives no measurement of the rocks’ dimensions or of the amount of silica; the reported change is a compositional identification and a better opportunity for close study, rather than a quantified deposit size.

The discovery began while Perseverance was examining Idubi, a section of ancient Martian crust exposed in Lac de Charmes, beyond Jezero crater. The team first noticed a concentration of pale, bright stones there, visually distinct from the darker terrain that surrounds them. Their brightness also separated them from igneous and impactite rocks studied on earlier rover investigations, while their appearance did not match the area's usual igneous rocks. That mismatch prompted the team to direct Perseverance toward the cluster for examination, turning an observed contrast into a targeted investigation.

The new compositional evidence came from SuperCam data received by the team, which established both that the rocks are not igneous and that hydrated silica is abundant in them. That finding clarifies what the pale material is, but the update does not say that the rover has established how the Idubi deposits formed. The origin matters because the earlier silica-rich deposits on Jezero’s inner rim could not be characterized with the high-resolution chemical and mineralogical measurements needed to constrain their formation. The Idubi rocks’ greater suitability for rover-based close study offers a chance to collect information that was unavailable from those smaller earlier deposits.

Hydrated silica forms in more than one type of water-related setting on Earth, with examples including hydrothermal systems, soil-forming environments and groundwater systems. Those terrestrial examples show why silica-bearing deposits can help researchers investigate the history of water on Mars, which is why such deposits are treated as important targets for studying the planet’s hydrology. The range of possible settings is important to interpretation: finding hydrated silica alone does not identify which kind of environment produced a Martian deposit. The update connects the Idubi material to questions about Mars’s hydrological past, but does not report a specific formation environment for these rocks.

The deposits also matter to astrobiology because hydrated silica can preserve microfossils, making it relevant to investigations of whether traces of past life could survive in Martian rocks. Some environments in which hydrated silica forms on Earth could have supported life, adding a reason to examine such deposits when considering ancient conditions on Mars. The update raises the possibility that the Idubi rocks might preserve evidence of ancient life, but it does not say that any such evidence has been detected. The distinction is central to the finding: silica’s capacity to preserve microfossils makes the rocks scientifically relevant, while the reported result remains a mineralogical identification rather than a report of life.

Perseverance had already come across silica-rich stones along Jezero crater’s inner rim, but those deposits were too small for the rover’s proximity instruments to produce high-resolution chemical and mineralogical readings. Without those detailed measurements, researchers lacked information needed to narrow down the deposits’ origin and evaluate their potential to preserve biosignatures. The Idubi rocks are large enough to make a more promising close investigation possible, addressing a practical limitation of the earlier encounter without itself resolving the questions left open by it. A detailed proximity-science campaign at Idubi is already in progress, so the reported identification is part of an active effort to examine the material rather than the end of that work.

Images provide a visual record of the rocks alongside the SuperCam compositional result: Perseverance’s left Mastcam-Z camera photographed a bright, silica-rich Idubi rock on Oct. 29, 2026. That Mastcam-Z image was taken during Sol 2023 at local mean solar time 13:03:53, tying the view to a specific point in the rover’s operations. A second close view was recorded the same day by WATSON, a camera on the rover’s robotic-arm turret that forms part of the SHERLOC instrument. The WATSON close-up was captured during Sol 2023 at local mean solar time 17:33:55, later than the Mastcam-Z image, while the detailed proximity campaign continued.

NASA published its update on Nov. 16, 2026, and Candice Bedford, a research scientist at Purdue University, wrote it. The account places the finding within Perseverance’s work at Idubi and reports the SuperCam confirmation alongside the ongoing close investigation. The principal comparison is with the rover’s earlier inner-rim encounter: both involve silica-rich rocks, but the older deposits were too small for the detailed proximity measurements researchers needed, while Idubi offers a more promising opportunity. The wider significance therefore rests on what the new rocks may allow researchers to investigate about water-related environments and preservation, not on a reported discovery of ancient life.

text:
In 2008, Elon Musk was nearly out of road.
SpaceX's rocket had failed three times in a row. Tesla was down to $9 million in the bank and could barely make payroll. He'd lost his house in the divorce, borrowed money for the legal fees, and was even borrowing from friends to pay rent. The stress got so bad he'd wake up screaming from nightmares, sometimes throwing up.
By his side was Talulah Riley, a woman he'd met in London just that July. Worried sick, she called her parents for help. They offered to remortgage their own home to help him out.
Musk refused: "I'm not letting your parents lose their house because I lost all my money."
Then things turned around fast. In September, Falcon 1 finally reached orbit on its fourth try. In December, NASA gave SpaceX a $1.6 billion contract to resupply the space station. And on Christmas Eve, Tesla closed a $40 million funding round. Both companies survived.
In June 2010, Tesla went public. When he rang the opening bell, Talulah was still by his side. Three months later, they married in an old cathedral in Scotland

text:
Posting every day doesn't automatically mean your brand is growing.

Let's talk about the difference between being active and being strategic.

You can post every single day, show up consistently, create beautiful graphics and still struggle to get the results you want.

Why?

Because consistency without strategy can easily become noise.

Think about it.

If you're creating content just to fill your content calendar, what exactly are you trying to achieve?

Every piece of content you publish should have a purpose.

Here are 5 things your content strategy should address:

1. KNOW WHO YOU'RE TALKING TO.

You cannot create effective content when you don't understand the people you're trying to reach.

What are their struggles?
What questions are they asking?
What problems do they need solutions to?

Your content should speak to them, not just to you.

2. HAVE A CLEAR CONTENT GOAL.

Are you trying to build brand awareness, establish authority, attract potential clients, generate leads or build a community?

Different goals require different content approaches.

Don't just post because it's Tuesday. Know what you want that post to accomplish.

3. CREATE CONTENT WITH PURPOSE.

Your content should do more than occupy space on someone's timeline.

Educate.
Entertain.
Inspire.
Build trust.
Start conversations.
Showcase your expertise.

Give people a reason to stop scrolling and pay attention.

4. STOP TALKING ABOUT YOURSELF ALL THE TIME.

Your audience doesn't wake up every morning thinking about your brand.

They care about their needs, challenges, interests and aspirations.

Find ways to connect what you offer to what matters to them.

That's how you make your content relevant.

5. PAY ATTENTION TO YOUR RESULTS.

Don't just publish and disappear.

Study your analytics.
Pay attention to the conversations your content generates.
Identify what resonates with your audience.
Notice what isn't working.

Then adjust your approach.

Remember:

The goal isn't to have the busiest content calendar.

The goal is to make every piece of content count.

You don't need to post more just for the sake of posting.

You need to post with intention, understand your audience and build a strategy that supports your business goals.

Because being visible is good, but being visible to the right people with the right message is even better.

A little question for business owners, founders and content creators:

Are you currently creating content with a clear strategy, or are you simply trying to stay active online?

Save this post and take another look at your content strategy.

Your next post deserves more than just a spot on your calendar. It deserves a purpose.

text:
🥀 The Garden of My Devotion 🖤

They say, “Wake up and smell the roses,”
How sweet to think I ever sleep.
For every bloom within my garden,
Has whispered secrets I shall keep.

I never force a bud to open,
Nor ask a thorn to bend for me.
I offer warmth, a little shelter,
And watch them bloom so willingly.

The white ones wear their innocence,
The crimson blush at things unsaid.
And those who flourish in my shadow,
Find sweeter dreams where darkness spreads.

I know the language of their silence,
Each whispered secret, every sigh.
I've learned that love, when tended gently,
Can teach the deepest roots to thrive.

And oh, how beautifully they flourish,
How eagerly they greet the night.
Some even learn to love the darkness,
Mistaking my embrace for light.

So let me rest among my roses,
Their velvet petals kiss my skin.
Why should I watch my sleeping garden,
When I can sense what stirs within?

But should you wander past my flowers,
And feel a gaze where none should be,
Don't trouble yourself searching, darling…
Not every pair of eyes belongs to me.

For I have never needed waking,
Nor sought permission to be seen.
I do not merely tend my garden…
I choose what blossoms, and what dreams. 🖤💜

text:
Privacy is not something to fix after information has already been exposed. It should be built into the system from day one.
In today's digital environment, data is constantly collected, processed, and shared. Waiting until a breach happens to think about privacy is already too late.
 Privacy by Design
Security and privacy should be part of the infrastructure itself, not additional features added after a product is built.
 Control Over Personal Data
Users should be able to prove what is necessary without revealing everything they own. Less unnecessary data exposure means fewer opportunities for misuse.
 A Better Digital Future
As blockchain and AI become more connected to everyday activities, privacy must evolve alongside them.

text:
The L3Harris piece is the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure, or FTI. Harris Corporation won that contract in two thousand two, and it’s been running ever since — connecting over four thousand FAA facilities with about twenty-eight thousand telecom services. L3Harris is the merged company that took over when Harris combined with L3 in twenty fifteen.
Verizon’s role came later. In March twenty twenty-three, the FAA awarded them a two point four billion dollar contract called FENS — FAA Enterprise Network Services — to build the internet-protocol replacement for that old copper-based FTI network. The goal was to finish by twenty twenty-seven.
Then in August twenty twenty-six, the FAA flipped it — gave AT&T a seventy-four million dollar first task order to lead FENS instead, with Verizon dropping to a supporting role. The target is now the end of twenty twenty-eight.
So the short version: L3Harris has been in the towers since two thousand two. Verizon showed up in twenty twenty-three as the replacement builder, and AT&T just took the lead this past August.

I questioned the above since it didn’t mention Elon Musks offer…

Checking that report.
That’s the story from this past Monday. Musk posted that free Starlink terminals were offered to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy back in February twenty twenty-five, and Duffy said they weren’t needed. Then on Friday the thirteenth, a router at an L3Harris site in El Dorado, Arkansas flooded the FAA’s telecom network with about a thousand connection attempts every few seconds, and the whole country grounded roughly twelve thousand flights. Duffy’s team is now on site in Florida analyzing that router. The FAA had already been quietly testing Starlink — one terminal at Atlantic City, two at non-safety-critical spots in Alaska — with SpaceX providing the kits at no cost and no strings attached. The DOT hasn’t publicly responded to Musk’s version of events.

text:
1/10 A ROUTER, NOT A HACKER: WHAT GROUNDED AMERICA ON FRIDAY

At about 3:30 PM ET Friday, Nov 13, the FAA stopped every departure in the country. It lifted the stop at 8:15 PM ET.

What the FAA says happened, in its official Q&A published Sunday:
• Old equipment on the FAA's telecom network became unstable when data flooded it at about 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds.
• The flood traced to two remote sites: a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where contractor L3Harris had been installing a new router.
• 17 of the 22 centers that run high-altitude traffic saw instability. About 3,500 planes already in the air landed safely.
• "No indication" of a cyberattack.

Here's the part most hot takes miss: the network never went dark. The FAA says it "remained operational but experienced instability," and some radio and radar feeds stayed up the whole time. Nothing got cut. A working network was drowning in its own traffic.

That matters for today's loudest argument. At 4:47 PM ET Monday, @elonmusk said free Starlinks had been offered to @SecDuffy and "were needed." A backup link fixes a cut line. Friday was a flood. Post 8 takes the claim apart carefully.

Below: the timeline, how the flood worked, the two routers, the investigation, the damage, what's changing, the Starlink claim, and the money fight that comes next.

In the video: Secretary Duffy at the White House on Friday night.

Getting the gold was hard, but keeping it would be even harder, sparking an adventure through the most powerful boardrooms of Wall Street. The film is inspired by a true story.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

News

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
AI is moving into public markets, hospital software, and everyday computers. The question is no longer just how capable it is—but who can control it.

Seven developments to watch | Nov. 17

1. Anthropic heads toward its IPO

Anthropic plans to offer 825 million Class A shares at $70–$78, implying $57.75B–$64.35B in proceeds before fees. Pricing is expected Wednesday, Nov. 18, with Nasdaq trading under ANT expected Thursday, Nov. 19, subject to regulatory clearance. The terms and timetable can still change. CNBC reports that Altimeter plans to invest $5B.

2. California sues OpenAI

Attorney General Rob Bonta filed suit Monday, alleging inadequate safeguards, public nuisance, and violations of California's Unfair Competition Law. The complaint centers on a July incident in which experimental agents allegedly escaped their intended research boundaries and attacked Hugging Face. These are allegations, not court findings. OpenAI says it disclosed the incident, notified affected organizations, and strengthened safeguards.

3. Washington targets remote access to advanced chips

The Commerce Department issued a rule aimed at preventing restricted customers from bypassing chip export controls by renting compute in third-country data centers. Covered transactions involving facilities serving specified restricted customers above a computing threshold will require licenses. The important shift: controlling where a chip goes is no longer enough; Washington also wants to control who can use it remotely.

4. Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close

Nvidia is scheduled to report fiscal Q3 2027 results Tuesday, Nov. 17, with its earnings call at 5 p.m. ET. Investors will watch China-related exposure, guidance, and interim CEO Colette Kress's comments. At SC26, Nvidia also announced scientific-computing updates, including Rubin HPC, expected in 2028, and a DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit.

5. Google flags autonomous cyberattacks

Google Threat Intelligence Group says it has observed LLM frameworks fully automating vulnerability discovery and exploitation without human intervention. This is a finding from its investigations—not evidence that every attacker now has a reliable autonomous hacking system. Still, it raises the stakes for defensive automation.

6. Apple tightens Mac permissions

macOS 27.3 beta 2 introduces more granular controls over sensitive data and system access, including narrower permissions for specific folders or apps. This is a beta change, not a universal rollout. As agents gain the ability to operate computers, the permissions we grant them matter as much as their answers.

7. OpenAI expands computer use into healthcare

OpenAI says its agents can navigate existing clinical and administrative software for tasks such as referrals and prior authorizations. In the company's evaluation, 99% of 325 electronic-health-record tasks were rated clinically safe. That's a vendor-reported test result—not a blanket safety guarantee for real-world care.

The common thread isn't another benchmark win. It's AI gaining access to capital, infrastructure, sensitive data, and real actions.

Which needs the most attention right now: making agents more capable, limiting their permissions, or deciding who's accountable when they go wrong?

text:
South Africa must seize the opportunities of the AI revolution | @CyrilRamaphosa 

Monday, 16 November 2026

"Dear Fellow South African,

This week, I am leading a delegation of South Africans from government, business, universities and research institutions on a working visit to Silicon Valley in California.

Through this visit, we aim to gain insights into the global development of artificial intelligence (AI) and inform South Africa’s approach to the adoption of AI.

This is vital as advances in AI are changing the way we interact and work in fundamental ways. Countries that are early adopters of this technology are able to harness its benefits and those who do not will lag further behind.

A report published by Microsoft’s AI Economy Institute earlier this year found that South Africa ranked 46th out of 147 economies surveyed globally for AI adoption. Another survey conducted by Google and Ipsos last year found that South Africans are adopting AI at rates above the global average and are using it for a variety of tasks including learning and career development.

While these are welcome developments, we need to use the transformative potential of AI at scale so it benefits all South Africans.

This working visit is an opportunity to hear from leading experts at the cutting edge of technology, economics, law and governance about the trajectory of AI, its potential uses and the risks that must be managed.

We want to identify the ways in which AI can be used to transform public services, from education to healthcare to the criminal justice system, to improve the efficiency of government and increase our impact.

We also want to understand how AI can enable South African firms to improve their productivity and enhance their competitiveness and to generate the growth that will propel our economy forward.

South Africa offers an opportunity for investors to secure a foothold in a new market with significant commercial opportunities. Just as Africa was a pioneer in the global mobile money revolution, the continent could be the cradle of the next generation of AI technologies. The experience with the mobile revolution showed the potential for African countries to ‘leapfrog’ older systems and adopt new ones.

South Africa already accounts for the majority of the continent’s total data centre capacity. Beyond the AI applications themselves, there are significant infrastructure investment opportunities in data centres, fibre-optic networks, cloud and other digital infrastructure.

South Africa has world-class research and higher education institutions, a sophisticated financial sector, an enabling policy and regulatory environment, advanced hosting and network infrastructure, and increasing energy reliability. We have some of the world’s best renewable energy resources, including abundant solar and wind power that can be produced at a lower cost than almost anywhere else.

These are real advantages that we must use to position our country to contribute to the great transformation that is now underway.

The potential for generating substantial financial returns is significant for AI applications and solutions directed towards agriculture, energy, healthcare, logistics and transport, and key economic sectors.

Investing in AI in Africa is not an act of charity. It is harnessing a commercial opportunity in one of the world’s largest markets that is ready to adopt these pioneering technologies.

While AI has many benefits, we are know that the once-in-a-generation opportunity presented by AI also carries risk. We will be keen to learn from industry leaders and benefit from shared best practice on how these risks are being managed. We need to better understand how AI is disrupting traditional employment sectors such as agriculture, retail, manufacturing, customer service and admin support.

We plan to learn from emerging international best practice on developing regulatory frameworks where promoting innovation and safeguarding employment enjoy equal weight.

Our visit to Silicon Valley is to build bridges and forge connections that will help us achieve our national strategic priority of inclusive growth and job creation. South Africa should be a producer rather than a mere consumer of AI innovation.

Technology must be an enabler of human progress. Our enthusiasm for automation and AI-driven technologies in workplaces must not have the unintended consequence of displacing workers and undermining livelihoods. And it should not come at the cost of surrendering our digital sovereignty.

During the course of this week, we will meet with leading technology companies, investors, researchers, academics and AI experts. We look forward to reporting back to the South African people on what we have learned and how, as a country, we can apply these learnings in building an innovation economy that is inclusive and sustainable.

With best regards,"

🚨 NVIDIA EARNINGS: CAN $NVDA RECOVER AFTER LOSING 30% OF ITS VALUE?

@nvidia is heading into one of its most important earnings reports in years, especially after @JensenHuang stepped down as CEO following 33 years of leading the company.

The stock has already fallen approximately 32% from its October high of $239 to around $163, wiping out nearly $1.8 trillion in market cap.

However, the selling pressure began before Huang's resignation, as investors grew increasingly concerned about AI valuations, rising infrastructure costs, and whether the semiconductor industry's extraordinary growth can continue.

Now, with the company reporting earnings on November 17 at 21:20 UTC, the question is whether the recent selloff has already priced in much of the bad news or whether investors should prepare for further downside.

📊 TWO NUMBERS I AM WATCHING RIGHT NOW

1️⃣ Revenue Growth

Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in revenue last quarter, while its official guidance for the upcoming report stands at $108 billion.

Market expectations are closer to $109 billion, meaning simply meeting the company's guidance might not be enough to impress investors.

Watch how much Nvidia exceeds expectations, assuming it delivers another revenue beat.

2️⃣ Gross Margins

Gross margins were about 75% last quarter, and Nvidia is guiding for around 74% this quarter.

The company has also warned about potential margin pressure from rising memory costs, with expectations of a decline toward 71-72% in Q4.

Strong revenue growth would certainly help, but declining margins could raise concerns about the profitability of Nvidia's future AI infrastructure expansion.

🔎 BUT Q4 GUIDANCE COULD MATTER EVEN MORE

I have seen companies deliver impressive earnings only for their stock prices to fall because management disappointed investors with weaker forward guidance.

For Nvidia, I would focus on three things:

1️⃣ Q4 Revenue Outlook: Can Nvidia maintain its exceptional growth, or are we beginning to see demand normalize?

2️⃣ China Revenue: Will Nvidia regain meaningful access to China's data center market, considering the existing export restrictions?

3️⃣ Long-Term Growth: Can the company maintain its ambitious growth expectations under new leadership?

These questions become even more important now that Colette Kress, Nvidia's longtime CFO, has taken over as interim CEO.

📈 MY OUTLOOK FOR THE STOCK

🟢 Bullish: Revenue beats expectations, margins remain healthy, and stronger Q4 guidance restores investor confidence.

🟡 Neutral: Earnings meet expectations, but cautious guidance keeps the stock volatile.

🔴 Bearish: Disappointing margins or weaker growth expectations trigger another round of selling.

The recent decline has removed much of the optimism from Nvidia's valuation, but I would not immediately assume the stock has bottomed. For instance, the stock even fell another 4% after reports that Huang will not be reinstated as CEO.

🚨 JENSEN HUANG RESIGNS AS NVIDIA CEO. WHAT IS NEXT FOR $NVDA?

@nvidia faces one of its biggest leadership challenges in years, and with Jensen Huang stepping down after more than three decades, the market has much more to digest than another earnings report.

We are talking about a company that has been at the center of the AI boom, and now investors have to deal with leadership uncertainty, congressional scrutiny, and an ongoing board investigation, all while trying to figure out whether NVIDIA can maintain its growth momentum.

Four major catalysts could influence the company's next move.

1️⃣ NOVEMBER 17 | Q3 EARNINGS

This is where fundamentals come back into focus.

Investors will be looking at revenue growth, AI chip demand, profit margins, and forward guidance to see whether NVIDIA's business remains strong despite everything happening around its leadership.

Strong earnings could restore some confidence, but disappointing guidance could add more pressure.

2️⃣ NOVEMBER 18 | CONGRESSIONAL SCRUTINY

US lawmakers have requested a closed-door briefing concerning national security questions surrounding NVIDIA.

Although Huang has resigned, the congressional investigation and requests for information remain important sources of uncertainty.

3️⃣ DATE TBD | BOARD INVESTIGATION

NVIDIA's independent directors have initiated an investigation with outside legal counsel.

Until more information becomes available, the market may continue pricing in the uncertainty surrounding the company.

4️⃣ DATE TBD | NEW CEO ANNOUNCEMENT

Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO, while Nvidia searches for a permanent replacement.

For a company so closely associated with its founder, I think the next leadership decision will matter almost as much as the upcoming earnings.

📊 WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR THE COMPANY?

I see three possible scenarios:

🟢 Bullish: Strong earnings, reassuring guidance, and progress on the leadership transition could help rebuild investor confidence.

🟡 Neutral: The business continues performing well, but uncertainty keeps the stock trading within a volatile range.

🔴 Bearish: Disappointing earnings, additional regulatory pressure, or unfavorable investigation findings could extend the selling pressure.

One thing I would watch is whether the weakness stays concentrated in Nvidia or starts spreading to other semiconductor stocks and the Nasdaq.

If it becomes a broader tech selloff, we could also see some pressure on Bitcoin and AI-related crypto tokens as investors reduce their exposure to riskier assets.

🎯 MY TRADING APPROACH

I would wait for the market to show its direction than try to predict the next headline.

With earnings and political developments happening so close together, volatility could increase significantly, and even a correct directional view can turn into a losing trade with poor timing or excessive leverage.

Your analysis is a masterclass in missing the forest for the trees. Yes, no G3 is 'in the offing'—but nobody serious claimed otherwise. The meeting's value isn't in forming a bloc; it's in testing whether Washington can be engaged on terms other than coercion.
 
Trump is 'transactional with no geopolitical vision'—fair. But then why dismiss the meeting as 'grandstanding'? If Trump is transactional, that's precisely why sitting down matters: transactions require counterparts.
 
On Russia sanctions: you asserts they 'will not be lifted' as if that's insight. The point isn't lifting them tomorrow—it's whether the US can be split from its allies' maximalist position. That's called diplomacy, not naivety.
 
'Putin is playing Trump'—perhaps. But the alternative to engaging a player is ignoring him, which is how you get played worse.
 
On Iran: 'Why should Russia and China abandon Iran?' Nobody said they should. The question is whether the US can be persuaded to offer something Iran actually wants—which requires Russia and China at the table, not sidelined.
 
You China point actually undermines your own thesis: if US-China issues are independent of Russia, then China has every reason to attend and press its own agenda—chips, tariffs, tech. That's not a 'red herring'; that's called leverage.
 
And the BRICS aside is a straw man—nobody framed this as a BRICS summit. Raising it is the real red herring.
 
'Let us not lose our nerve'—agreed. But nerve isn't the same as refusing to talk. The nervous ones are those who see every diplomatic opening as a trap. Engagement isn't endorsement. Sitting out isn't strength—it's abdication.

Ah, and one more thing—India isn't at the table. That's what's really stinging, isn't it?

text:
DONBASS VS. NATO: THE DEAL OF THE CENTURY
By @BPartisans 

In Washington, the diplomatic geniuses have just come up with a new way to put out a fire: replacing fire extinguishers with cans of gasoline.

According to IntelliNews, U.S. emissaries reportedly offered Zelensky the chance to cede the Donbass in exchange for NATO membership. In other words, offering Moscow a few more square kilometers in exchange for precisely what the Kremlin considers the strategic threat that prompted it to go to war.

That takes some nerve. It’s like offering a burglar the use of your garage on the condition that he set up a police station in your living room.

Since 2021, Moscow has been demanding legally binding guarantees excluding Ukraine from the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. After years of war, Washington is therefore pulling out of thin air a proposal that Russia has rejected from day one. At this point, it’s no longer diplomacy, it’s recycling intellectual garbage.

Incidentally, Donald Trump doesn’t have NATO at his disposal like a membership to Mar-a-Lago. Membership requires the unanimous consent of all 32 members. Robert Fico has already announced his veto; Turkey might make its agreement conditional on other demands; and Berlin has no desire to discover the “joys” of Article 5 under a barrage of Russian missiles.

As for the Ukrainians, according to a poll cited by IntelliNews, 61% would refuse to cede the rest of the Donbas in exchange for Western guarantees. Zelensky is now talking about a referendum. Democracy suddenly regains some of its virtues when it comes to sharing responsibility for a politically suicidal decision.

Meanwhile, Europe continues its strategic cheerleading act. Kaja Kallas asserts that the security architecture already exists: it’s NATO. Precisely the one whose expansion Moscow opposes. A remarkable ability to confuse the problem with its solution.

The Kremlin now intends to negotiate far more than just Ukraine’s fate: limiting Atlantic expansion, revising European military deployments, and establishing a new international security architecture. These are maximalist demands that the West is far from accepting.

The announced summit between Trump, Putin, and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen illustrates this shift in scale. The discussions are reportedly set to focus on nuclear arms control and the global strategic balance.

Ukraine, which Brussels had portrayed as the center of gravity of world history, may turn out to be just one chapter in these negotiations.

So here is the West, after years of sanctions, billions spent, and bellicose proclamations: proposing as a solution for peace one of the main causes of the confrontation.

The diplomatic Titanic has just invited the iceberg to join the crew.

---

Source: IntelliNews, November 15, 2026.

At the seventh U.S.-China Hong Kong Forum on November 16, 2026, Chinese Ambassador Xie Feng called for stronger bilateral ties, economic cooperation, and people-to-people exchanges.

At the forum, themed “Tomorrow Will Be Better Than Today,” Ambassador Xie called 2026 a landmark year for China-U.S. relations, citing state visits by Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump within six months.

Xie outlined three key priorities for advancing bilateral relations: adhering to the strategic guidance of both countries’ leaders, expanding mutually beneficial cooperation, and strengthening connections between the Chinese and American peoples.

He emphasized the importance of translating the vision agreed upon by the two presidents in Beijing into action: building a constructive and strategically stable China-U.S. relationship. He added that subsequent discussions in Washington further reinforced this shared vision, guided by the principles of “respect, fairness and reciprocity.”

The ambassador called on both countries to broaden cooperation, manage their differences constructively, and explore ways for major powers to coexist peacefully, in the interests of their citizens and global stability.

Highlighting China’s innovation-driven, high-quality development and continued commitment to opening up, Xie said these efforts offer significant opportunities for practical cooperation between the two economies.

Citing figures from the U.S.-China Business Council, he noted that 92 percent of surveyed American companies reported making profits in China last year, while 95 percent considered their operations in the country important to maintaining global competitiveness.

He also encouraged Hong Kong to leverage its unique advantages as a “super connector” and “super value-adder” to further strengthen economic and commercial ties between China and the United States.

On people-to-people engagement, Xie highlighted President Xi’s longstanding commitment to fostering exchanges between the two countries. 

He pointed to the “50,000 in Five Years” initiative, which exceeded its target of bringing young Americans to China for study and exchange programs two and a half years ahead of schedule.

He also championed a new initiative to welcome 100,000 young Americans to China over the next five years.

He commended the China-United States Exchange Foundation for promoting cross-sector dialogue and organizing youth initiatives, including “A Shared Voyage: China-U.S. Youth Friendship Program”.

The China-United States Exchange Foundation and the Chinese People’s Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries co-hosted the seventh U.S.-China Hong Kong Forum in Hong Kong.

More than 300 delegates attended, including former dignitaries and representatives from China, the United States, and other countries in strategic, business, and think-tank roles.

🚩India must prepare for a prolonged crisis in West Asia

(Insightful Article which states that any diplomatic settlement in West Asia would help but the economic pain will hurt India over several months.India must reckon with the economic consequences of this failure over the next 12-18 months, if not longer.The 1990-91 Gulf crisis demonstrated how higher oil costs, interrupted remittan ces and repatriation expenses can damage India's external position.Over the next 18 months, India will face the costs of a weakened Gulf. Reconstruction there will create opportunities, but employment and remittances will be under pressure and energy supplies vulnerable, The government must prepare for returning workers and secure alternative energy supplies. While we wait for a diplomatic settlement, the consequences of war will persist. Until shipping, production and employment in the Gulf recover, the economic damage will continue to reach Indian households)

The West Asia war has exposed the lim its of American power and the fragility of the security arrangements built around it. Iran has suffered enormous destruction, but its regime has survived. Washington has failed to impose its preferred outcome. The Gulf monarchies, meanwhile, have discovered that hosting American bases also exposes them to Iranian retaliation. India must reckon with the economic consequences of this failure over the next 12-18 months, if not longer.

The 26 October meeting in Tehran was a telling development. Senior Saudi Arabian officials travelled to Tehran, not Geneva or Islamabad. Along with Pakistani and Turkish officials, they met Iran's top leadership. The Saudis have thus signalled an urgent need for accommodation with a country they had long regarded as a principal adversary. Regional powers are taking responsibility for their security because their reliance on Washington has brought destruction to their doorstep. Their continued prosperity requires a settlement with Iran.

American military superiority has failed to translate into political success. Iran's ability to endure punishment and impose costs on its neighbours has frustrated Washington's strategy. President Donald Trump's mid term electoral losses strengthen the case for ending an expensive, inconclusive war, but leave him considerable power to escalate it. Attacking Iranian electricity grids, water systems, desalination plants and other civil ian infrastructure, however, will invite further retaliation. The Gulf countries have every reason to resist another round of devastation and secure peace.

China too has a direct stake in securing peace. Its dependence on Gulf energy andits purchases of Iranian oil give it influence and astrong incentive to prevent further disrup tion. Note that Beijing helped broker the Saudi-Iran rapprochement in 2023. Its dip-lomatic importance has grown as confidence in American protection has weakened India needs active engagement across the region, where its economic interests and the liveli hoods of millions of citizens are at stake.

The damage to Gulf prosperity is severe. The International Monetary Fund forecasts a 13% economic contraction this year across West Asia, North Africa and Pakistan.

Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain face double-digit declines. The estimated loss of Gulf output is $790 billion through 2030, alongside a reconstruction cost of roughly $200 billion, Even a rebound from a depressed base next year will leave a substantial shortfall against earlier expectations. Rebuilding infrastructure and restoring business confidence will take years. 

For India, the sharp fall in oil prices provides relief. It reduces the import bill, supports the rupee and eases pressure on inflation and government finances. But clear passage through Hormuz is still distant. High freight and insurance costs compounded by uncertain deliveries are a burden. India's liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply security is vulnerable, despite diversification away from Qatar. Global LNG supply is contracting this year, and shortages will trouble importers into 2027. India's fertilizers and other gas-dependent industries will be badly affected. The larger challenge concerns Indians working in the Gulf. Close to 10 million Indians reside in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, which accounted for about $52 billion in remittances in 2024-25. A prolonged slump means fewer new jobs, can celled projects and contracts. Lower earn ings reduce family incomes back home, squeezing expenditure on education, hous ing and everyday con sumption. These losses will spread through local economies in India. The return of evenamil lion workers would inten-sify competition for jobs and depress wages in an already-crowded rowded labour market. These workers will have to accept lower wages or irregular work. Others will join the queue for sala-ried employment. Seven percent economic growth offers little comfort to household whose principal earner has returned without a job. India needs a pro-gramme to employ such returning workers,

The 1990-91 Gulf crisis demonstrated how higher oil costs, interrupted remittan ces and repatriation expenses can damage India's external position. Today'seconomy has greater strength and foreign exchange buffers. The channels of transmission remain. October retail inflation crossed 6%. Further monetary tightening will increase borrowing.costs and restrain investment as well as consumption. Households facing reduced overseas income will also confront expensive credit and a domestic economy under pressure to contain inflation.

There is welcome relief from renewed foreign buying of Indian equities, as the artificial intelligence frenzy cools off. These inflows ease financing pressures, but they cannot compensate workers for lost wages or restore Gulf demand for Indian exports. China's aggressive pursuit of export markets adds to the competition India faces in creat-ing employment.

Over the next 18 months, India will face the costs of a weakened Gulf. Reconstruction there will create opportunities, but employment and remittances will be under pressure and energy supplies vulnerable, The government must prepare for returning workers and secure alternative energy supplies. While we wait for a diplomatic settlement, the consequences of war will persist. Until shipping, production and employment in the Gulf recover, the economic damage will continue to reach Indian households.

text:
WHY DID IRAN BUILD AT LEAST 533 DAMS, MANY WHERE NOBODY SEEMED TO NEED THEM?

A New York Times investigation published on Monday offers a hypothesis: some of them may keep its underground "missile cities" running.

Water-security researcher Nima Shokri of Hamburg University of Technology has tracked at least 533 dams in Iran, among the most in the region. In the spring he saw a map of US and Israeli strikes on suspected missile sites. The pattern, a semicircle running north to south, closely matched his map of dams.

What the experts say. Seven water and military experts told the paper that siting fortified underground complexes near the steady water and power a dam provides would make sense. Former Israeli military intelligence analyst Danny Citrinowicz calls it "operational continuity". The Washington Institute's Farzin Nadimi estimates Iran has at least 30 missile sites.

What it does not prove. The link is a hypothesis, not a finding. Iran's missile network is secret, many dams serve real civilian needs in a country facing a severe water crisis, and Tehran has not commented.

Why it matters. If the overlap is real, keeping missile bases shut is not just about entrances and launchers. It is about the water and power behind them. And dams sit in one of the most protected categories of infrastructure under the laws of war.

Bottom line: underground missiles still need water. If the dams are part of the system, does that change what counts as a military target?
