text:
While barefooted Ethiopian warriors under Emperor Yohannes IV and Ras Alula paid in blood and sacrifice at Gundet — standing against modern rifles, artillery, and European officers with little more than courage, terrain, and determination — today’s Tsimdo figures, backed by Egypt and Eritrea, choose the comfort of foreign capitals and street protests to work against the very nation those heroes defended.

Heroism that still echoes. 🇪🇹
One hundred and fifty years after the Battle of Gundet, questions continue to be raised about external actors seeking to influence Ethiopian affairs. Diaspora demonstrations in Washington and European capitals, while protected by free speech, do not substitute for engagement and solutions developed within Ethiopia itself.

History offers a clear lesson: lasting change has rarely been achieved solely through protests conducted from abroad. Figures such as Mandela and Gandhi pursued their struggles from within their own societies. The international community is well aware of the complex regional dynamics involving Ethiopia, Egypt, and Eritrea. Sustainable outcomes will depend on dialogue, mutual respect for sovereignty, and the ability of Ethiopians to shape their own future.

Working against the fundamental interests and security of one’s own country is a serious matter that many regard as treasonous. With the TPLF’s military and political capacity significantly weakened, some elements are now reportedly using Eritrean territory as a platform for activities directed against Ethiopia. These acts of hostility are widely understood to be encouraged and supported by Egypt. The Ethiopian government has a clear responsibility to protect the safety and security of its people. Consequently, it cannot be expected to leave unchecked any force that continues to pose a potential threat to national security. #Gundet150 #Ethiopia

text:
LAST WEEK NEWS-

NVIDIA IN CRISIS AFTER JENSEN HUANG’S RESIGNATION

Nvidia has been thrown into its most serious leadership crisis in years after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect.

The company named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Huang’s departure followed reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence agencies of having links to Chinese intelligence.

The resignation has shaken investors, employees and the wider AI industry, where Huang has been the public face of Nvidia’s rise into the dominant supplier of AI chips.

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #AI #TechNews #TheWorldCorrespondent

A MASSIVE CAMPAIGN TO BRING HIM BACK

A petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement quickly gathered more than 180,000 signatures, including thousands of current and former Nvidia employees and shareholders.

Elon Musk publicly backed the campaign, saying it would be an “honor” to hire Huang. Billionaire investor Leo KoGuan also said he would not invest further in Nvidia without Huang, while reports said two investors holding more than $2 billion in shares urged the board to reconsider.

However, Nvidia’s board has reportedly ruled out bringing Huang back as CEO or in any other role, despite the scale of the campaign.

#Nvidia #ElonMusk #StockMarket #CorporateGovernance #TheWorldCorrespondent

CRYPTO MARKETS TAKE A SHARP HIT

Bitcoin fell to $62,000 over the weekend, its lowest level since August, as a wave of forced liquidations swept through leveraged crypto positions.

The selloff came amid weaker liquidity, institutional selling and a broader decline in risk appetite. Bitcoin later rebounded toward $64,000, but the episode underlined how quickly leverage can turn a market downturn into a cascade of forced selling.

Reports of $5.9 billion in liquidations appear overstated or misattributed: exchange data cited by CNBC showed liquidations of roughly $165 million on Saturday, after $629 million on Friday and nearly $700 million on Thursday.

#Bitcoin #Crypto #Markets #Finance #TheWorldCorrespondent

AMERICA’S AIR TRAVEL SYSTEM BREAKS DOWN

The Federal Aviation Administration imposed a nationwide ground stop on Friday, halting nearly all departing flights for almost five hours after a communications failure affected air-traffic-control centers.

It was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001 attacks. Airlines canceled thousands of flights, and the disruption continued into the weekend as carriers struggled to restore schedules.

The incident exposed how fragile the country’s aviation infrastructure remains, even as air travel demand continues to grow.

#FAA #Aviation #USNews #Travel #TheWorldCorrespondent

SPACEX MAKES HISTORY WITH STARSHIP

SpaceX achieved a major milestone when it successfully caught Starship’s upper stage with the launch tower’s mechanical arms for the first time.

The catch followed Starship’s 15th test flight, during which the vehicle completed a 22-hour orbital journey before returning through the atmosphere and being recovered at Starbase, Texas.

The achievement is significant for SpaceX’s long-term goal of building a rapidly reusable launch system, although the Super Heavy booster itself was diverted to an offshore splashdown rather than recovered.

#SpaceX #Starship #Space #Innovation #TheWorldCorrespondent

AMERICAN HOUSEHOLDS FACE RECORD DEBT

US credit-card balances reached a record $1.29 trillion in the third quarter, rising by $22 billion from the previous quarter and $52 billion year on year, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

The rise comes as average credit-card interest rates remain near 20%, leaving many households exposed to mounting borrowing costs.

Senate Democrats, led by Senator Elizabeth Warren, are preparing legislation to cap credit-card interest rates at 10%. The proposal is not yet law, and it would still need to pass Congress and receive presidential approval.

#USEconomy #CreditCardDebt #ConsumerFinance #Politics #TheWorldCorrespondent

WALL STREET AND WASHINGTON SIGNAL CAUTION

Bank of America removed Nvidia and Micron from its list of top stock picks, while a Federal Reserve report identified artificial intelligence as one of the main risks facing the US financial system.

The moves reflect growing concern that valuations in AI-related stocks may have become disconnected from underlying earnings, cash flow and real economic demand.

For investors, the message is not necessarily that the AI boom is over. It is that concentration risk, leverage and inflated expectations can turn a technology success story into a market vulnerability.

#StockMarket #AI #FederalReserve #Investing #TheWorldCorrespondent

CRYPTO ENTERS THE REGULATED MAINSTREAM

Coinbase received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to charter Coinbase National Trust Company, placing its institutional crypto-custody business under a federal regulatory framework.

The approval allows Coinbase to offer digital-asset custody, settlement and stablecoin reserve management under OCC supervision. It is a major step in the normalization of crypto infrastructure within the US financial system.

Meanwhile, Deutsche Bank has launched crypto-custody services, and BlackRock has predicted that billions of dollars could move into crypto ETFs as investors seek regulated and secure exposure to digital assets.

#Coinbase #Crypto #DeutscheBank #BlackRock #TheWorldCorrespondent

text:
The larger question is what happens to American supply-chain security as Washington returns to a China policy centered on denial and exclusion. Beijing has spent the past six years learning how to respond to such measures, regardless of which party controls Washington.

China is already discouraging imports of Nvidia chips and does not appear to be encouraging commercial remote-access workarounds. 

And with some U.S. rare earth stockpiles reportedly at risk of reaching critically low levels as early as Q1 2027, Beijing’s leverage extends well beyond the rare earths and advanced materials currently commanding Washington’s attention. 

It encompasses critical minerals, processing technologies, specialized industrial inputs, and manufacturing capabilities on which American high-tech industries and defense production continue to depend.

The NSC may consider retaliation disproportionate and unwarranted, but Beijing is unlikely to assess its options according to Washington’s definition of proportionality. The last six years have shown ZNH that forbearance offers no dividend, but retaliation does.

Meanwhile, we’ve benched America’s starting AI quarterback while tightening restrictions on Chinese access to computing power based on older-generation GPUs, all in the middle of a defining technological competition.

That’s a curious strategy for a country that prides itself on winning. The America I know prefers setting itself up to win the game rather than celebrating artistic victories that come at the expense of tactical and strategic success.

Is that really the trade-off we intend to make? 🦉

That’s a curious strategy for a country that prides itself on winning. The America I know prefers setting itself up to win the game rather than celebrating artistic victories that come at the expense of tactical and strategic success.

Is that really the trade-off we intend to make? 🦉

text:
Long Post

 1 Kings 22:19–23

This passage is one of the most unusual descriptions of the heavenly world in the Hebrew Bible.

I want you to temporarily set aside the traditional assumption that every character in the passage is simply acting out a predetermined plan. Instead, let's read what the text actually describes.

1. Micaiah sees something happening in heaven

1 Kings 22:19:

"I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left."

Picture the scene.

There is a throne.
There is a central figure seated on it.
There is a heavenly assembly.
The heavenly beings are standing on either side.
A decision concerning an earthly king is about to be made.

This is not a description of an isolated God acting alone.

It is a picture of a royal heavenly court.

The Hebrew expression for the heavenly host is tseva ha-shamayim, the host or army of heaven.

The imagery resembles other divine-council passages, especially Job 1 and Psalm 82.

2. Something extraordinary happens: Yahweh asks a question

Verse 20:

"And the LORD said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?"

Notice the wording.

Yahweh asks the assembly:

Who will persuade Ahab?

He does not immediately announce how it will happen.

Instead, the heavenly assembly is presented with a question.

This is important because the narrative portrays a deliberative heavenly court.

It doesn't necessarily mean Yahweh lacks knowledge. A king can ask his council a question without needing information. But the author deliberately presents the decision as a heavenly consultation.

3. Different spirits offer different proposals

Verse 20 continues:

"And one said on this manner, and another said on that manner."

Think about that.

There are multiple participants in the heavenly assembly.

They are offering different proposals.

This is not a picture of identical angels mechanically carrying out instructions. It is a council in which heavenly beings participate in a discussion.

Then comes verse 21.

4. A spirit steps forward

Verse 21:

"And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the LORD, and said, I will persuade him."

This is the moment I want you to pay attention to.

The text says a spirit came forward.

It does not initially identify this spirit as Satan.

It is a member of the heavenly assembly who volunteers for a particular assignment.

Yahweh asks how he intends to accomplish it.

Verse 22:

"I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets."

Now consider the implications.

This spirit proposes to deceive the prophets of Ahab.

The spirit is not proposing to tell the truth. He is proposing to introduce deception into the earthly religious system.

And Yahweh responds:

"Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so."

The spirit receives permission.

This is a remarkable passage because it portrays a supernatural being proposing a course of action that Yahweh authorizes.

5. Who is this spirit?

There are several possibilities worth considering.

Possibility A: An obedient heavenly servant

The traditional interpretation sees the spirit as an agent of divine judgment. Ahab has repeatedly rejected truth, and the spirit becomes the instrument through which his judgment is carried out.

Possibility B: A morally ambiguous heavenly being

The narrative may be portraying a spirit whose methods are deceptive, but whose actions are incorporated into Yahweh's judgment.

Possibility C: A rebellious spiritual being

Some readers might wonder whether this spirit resembles Satan, or one of the rebellious heavenly beings described elsewhere.

There is an interesting parallel with Job.

In Job 1–2, Satan appears in the heavenly assembly and challenges the integrity of Job. Yahweh permits him to test Job within limits.

In 1 Kings 22, a spirit volunteers to deceive Ahab, and Yahweh permits it.

But we should not automatically identify the two spirits. The Hebrew word ruach simply means spirit, wind, or breath. The text never calls this particular spirit Satan.

6. Now look at the uncomfortable part

Verse 23:

"The LORD hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the LORD hath spoken evil concerning thee."

Micaiah explains the vision to Ahab.

The lying spirit is now part of the explanation for why Ahab's prophets are giving him false assurances.

Here is the theological problem:

If Yahweh authorizes the deception, who is responsible for the deception?

And if Ahab is being led toward death through false prophecy, what does that tell us about divine justice?

The passage forces us to confront the relationship between divine sovereignty, spiritual agents, deception, and human responsibility.

It is not an easy passage to reconcile with a simplistic picture in which God always operates through transparent and straightforward means.

7. Something even more important: Ahab is warned

Micaiah tells Ahab exactly what is happening.

Ahab now knows that his prophets are misleading him.

He has been given a warning.

But he chooses to reject it and sends Micaiah to prison.

Then Ahab goes into battle anyway.

He disguises himself, apparently hoping to avoid being targeted, but an unnamed archer shoots an arrow that strikes him between the joints of his armor.

He dies.

Read 1 Kings 22:29–38.

The story is presenting a judgment against a king who repeatedly rejects prophetic warnings.

But it leaves us with a difficult question: why does the heavenly court employ deception to accomplish that judgment?

8. Now compare this with the Book of Job

Satan appears before Yahweh.
A spirit appears before Yahweh.
Satan challenges Job's integrity.
The spirit proposes to deceive Ahab.

Yahweh permits a test.
Yahweh authorizes the spirit's proposal.

The heavenly being acts on earth.
The heavenly being acts through earthly prophets.
There is a recurring literary pattern:

A heavenly assembly, a supernatural participant, a proposal, divine permission, and consequences on earth.

This is important when we return to the question of whether Satan is necessarily God's opposite.

In Job, the Hebrew word ha-satan means the adversary or accuser. He functions as an accuser within the heavenly court.

That is different from the later Christian conception of Satan as the supreme enemy of God.

text:
🇨🇳 Camouflage on the battlefield: China puts its infantry tactics to the test

The increasing prevalence of reconnaissance and attack drones is forcing armed forces to fundamentally rethink their existing concepts of camouflage and cover. Even wooded terrain and traditional camouflage methods no longer offer reliable protection when enemy drones equipped with thermal imaging cameras and other sensors are in operation.

This problem became apparent during a tactical exercise by the 75th Army of the Southern Theatre Command of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA): An infantry platoon attempted to conceal itself in a wooded area using conventional methods. An enemy drone equipped with a thermal imaging camera detected the soldiers, transmitted their coordinates and enabled a simulated artillery strike. The entire platoon was subsequently deemed to have been wiped out.

The implications extend far beyond the procurement of new defence systems. The Chinese army is increasingly integrating drone defence into standard infantry training. In future, even ordinary soldiers are to be able to detect enemy drones, warn of their presence, deploy electronic countermeasures and engage them. Specialised training centres, simulators and realistic training scenarios are designed to impart these skills.

Crucially, this involves a fundamental shift in the conduct of combat. It is no longer sufficient to integrate drones into existing formations whilst the infantry continues to operate according to traditional principles. Movement patterns, the establishment of positions, camouflage and the use of the terrain must also be adapted to constant aerial surveillance.

The war in Ukraine has highlighted this development particularly clearly. Thermal imaging cameras, small reconnaissance drones and FPV systems can detect even well-camouflaged soldiers and prepared positions. In addition to the optical signature, heat signature, movements and other tell-tale characteristics also become a problem.

Traditional camouflage does not therefore lose its importance, but is no longer sufficient on its own as a protective concept. Armed forces must rethink their entire camouflage and survival doctrine: from the individual infantryman through to the construction of positions and the movement of entire formations. The battlefield of the future demands not only that forces conceal themselves from the enemy’s view, but also that they remain capable of operating whilst under constant drone surveillance.

text:
Magda Goebbels (born Johanna Maria Magdalena Ritschel) was the wife of Nazi Germany's propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels and a prominent figure in the Third Reich, often referred to as its unofficial "first lady". Her life traced an extraordinary and dark path from a youth with connections to Jewish and Zionist circles to fanatical devotion to Adolf Hitler and the destruction of her own family...

Born in Berlin, Magda attended high school and formed an early romantic relationship with Chaim Arlosoroff, a Jewish Zionist leader. In 1921, she married wealthy German industrialist Günther Quandt, with whom she had a son named Harald. The marriage was unhappy and ended in a high-profile divorce in 1929, leaving her financially independent.

In 1930, Magda attended a Nazi rally in Berlin and became captivated by the rhetoric of Joseph Goebbels. She joined the Nazi Party on 1 September 1930 and began working in party archives and managing Goebbels' personal papers. Magda and Joseph Goebbels married on 19 December 1931, with Adolf Hitler attending as a witness. Because Hitler chose to remain unmarried to cultivate his image as wedded to Germany, Magda was positioned as a glamorous, upper-class hostess and model "Aryan" mother for the regime. Despite their public image as the premier family of the Third Reich, the marriage suffered from Joseph's frequent infidelities—most notably his affair with Czech actress Lída Baarová—and Hitler personally intervened to block Magda's attempts to divorce him in 1938. Magda also engaged in her own extramarital relationships, such as with Karl Hanke.

As WWII collapsed and Soviet forces closed in on Berlin in April 1945, Magda brought her six children into Hitler’s Führerbunker. On 1 May 1945, a day after Hitler died by suicide, Magda had a doctor administer morphine and cyanide capsules to her six children (Helga, Hilde, Helmut, Holdine, Hedda and Heide) while they slept, killing all of them. Magda and Joseph Goebbels then walked up to the Chancellery garden and died by suicide via gunshot (with cyanide also utilized) and their bodies were burned.

. . . 

On April 28, 1945, fifty feet beneath the burning rubble of Berlin inside Adolf Hitler's concrete Führerbunker, forty-three-year-old Magda Goebbels sat down at a small desk to write a farewell letter to the only child she planned to let live. Outside, Soviet Red Army artillery shook the ceiling dust onto her stationery as Russian troops fought street by street toward the Reich Chancellery. Inside the cramped underground chambers, her six young children with Nazi Propaganda Minister Joseph Goebbels—Helga, Hildegard, Helmut, Holdine, Hedwig, and four-year-old Heidrun—played quietly in white nightclothes, unaware that their mother had already sealed their fate. Addressing the envelope to Harald Quandt, her twenty-three-year-old son from her first marriage who was then sitting in an Allied prisoner-of-war camp in North Africa, Magda laid out the chilling ideological logic behind one of the darkest acts of the Third Reich.

For more than a decade, Magda Goebbels had been celebrated by Nazi propaganda as the idealized "First Lady" of Germany—an elegant, photogenic mother whose blonde, blue-eyed children appeared regularly in newsreels and birthday greetings to Hitler. Devoted fanatically to the Führer, she had moved her entire family into the bunker on April 22, refusing to flee to Bavaria even as Berlin was encircled.

Over the next week, several high-ranking figures inside the compound—including Armaments Minister Albert Speer, Hitler's secretaries, and daring Luftwaffe test pilot Hanna Reitsch—pleaded with Magda to let them smuggle the six children out of the besieged capital to safety. Magda flatly rejected every rescue offer, telling Reitsch that her children belonged to the Third Reich and to Hitler, and insisting it was better for them to die than grow up in a defeated Germany stripped of National Socialism.

Me: Stoner

Ai: Stoner by John Williams is a literary novel published in 1965 that explores the quiet complexities of an ordinary man's life, examining love, ambition, disappointment, loneliness, and the search for meaning. Although initially overlooked, the novel has since become widely celebrated as a masterpiece of American literature.
The story follows William Stoner, a young man born into a poor farming family in rural Missouri at the end of the nineteenth century. Sent to the University of Missouri to study agriculture, he unexpectedly discovers a passion for literature and philosophy. This discovery transforms the direction of his life, leading him to abandon farming and pursue an academic career as an English professor.
Through Stoner's experiences, the novel traces his journey through marriage, fatherhood, professional rivalries, romantic relationships, and personal struggles. His life is marked by missed opportunities, emotional isolation, unfulfilled ambitions, and circumstances he often feels powerless to change. Yet beneath the apparent ordinariness of his existence lies a profound commitment to education, literature, and intellectual integrity.
One of the novel's central themes is the idea that a life does not need to be extraordinary to be meaningful. Williams explores the quiet dignity of perseverance, the limitations of human choice, the complexity of relationships, and the ways in which personal fulfillment can emerge from seemingly insignificant experiences.

Why read this book?
Self-discovery: Explores how discovering one's true interests can fundamentally change the direction of a life.
Purpose and meaning: Examines whether an ordinary life can still be considered a meaningful and successful one.
Human relationships: Offers a deeply realistic portrayal of marriage, love, family, friendship, and emotional distance.
Resilience: Illustrates the importance of maintaining personal convictions despite disappointment and adversity.
The value of knowledge: Celebrates literature, education, intellectual curiosity, and the lifelong pursuit of understanding.

Overall: Stoner is a deeply moving meditation on the human condition. It reminds readers that greatness is not always measured by wealth, recognition, achievement, or social status. Sometimes it is found in the quiet pursuit of what one loves, the ability to endure life's disappointments, and the courage to remain faithful to one's inner values. It is a particularly powerful book for anyone interested in understanding human nature, personal identity, and what it truly means to live a life.

🚨🗣️ Luis Suárez finally opens up on leaving Liverpool for Barcelona in 2014: “I would have given anything to win the Premier League with Steven Gerrard.”

“Liverpool gave me something special. When I arrived from Ajax, the supporters accepted me and made me feel at home. I played with hunger, anger and passion. Steven Gerrard was more than a captain to me. When Arsenal came calling, he told me not to rush into anything because he believed a bigger opportunity would eventually arrive. He made me feel wanted at Liverpool.

“The 2013/14 season still hurts. Daniel Sturridge, Raheem Sterling, Philippe Coutinho, Jordan Henderson and Gerrard. We were scoring goals for fun. I won the Golden Boot, PFA Player of the Year and Football Writers’ Player of the Year, but the Premier League title escaped us. We were so close. I wanted to give those supporters that trophy, but Man City had other plans.

“Then Barcelona came calling. Messi, Neymar, Xavi, Iniesta, Busquets and Piqué. I couldn’t turn that opportunity down. I won the Champions League, La Liga and the Copa del Rey. Playing alongside Messi and Neymar was incredible. But leaving Liverpool meant walking away from unfinished business.

“Then came 2019. We arrived at Anfield with a 3-0 advantage from the first leg. No Salah, no Firmino, and we genuinely believed we were going to the final. But Jürgen Klopp had other ideas. Origi, Wijnaldum, Shaqiri, Henderson, Milner and Trent Alexander-Arnold turned that stadium into something I had never experienced. When that fourth goal went in, I couldn’t believe it. I knew exactly what that comeback meant to Liverpool, but experiencing it as their opponent was heartbreaking.

“I have played with Messi, Neymar, Busquets and Jordi Alba. I’ve won almost everything football can offer. Now I’m enjoying another chapter with Inter Miami, reunited with Leo and enjoying life in the United States. But sometimes I think about Gerrard, that Liverpool dressing room and what we could have achieved together. I left to chase the biggest trophies, but I never stopped carrying #LFC with me.

“I WON THE CHAMPIONS LEAGUE WITH BARCELONA. BUT I NEVER GOT TO LIFT THE PREMIER LEAGUE TROPHY WITH STEVEN GERRARD AT ANFIELD. SOMETIMES, THE TROPHIES YOU WIN ARE NOT THE ONES YOU REMEMBER THE MOST.”

ONCE A RED, ALWAYS A RED.

PART 1

MY NEIGHBOR REJECTED AN OFFER THAT WAS $80,000 HIGHER THAN EVERY OTHER BID ON HIS HOUSE.

His wife thought he was making a terrible mistake. His children were furious. Even his real estate agent struggled to understand his decision.

But when I eventually learned why he turned it down, I understood something about him that I hadn't before.

Frank and his wife had lived in their Ohio home for 27 years. They raised two children there, celebrated birthdays in the backyard and hosted Thanksgiving dinners that seemed to get bigger every year.

Now their children were grown, and maintaining a four-bedroom house had become exhausting. They wanted to downsize and enjoy retirement.

So they put the property on the market.

The first few offers were reasonable. Then a developer came along with an offer that was $80,000 above the next highest bid.

Frank's wife was delighted.

Their agent called it an exceptional opportunity.

But Frank asked the buyer one question:

"What are you planning to do with the property?"

The buyer didn't hide his intentions. He wanted to demolish the house and redevelop the lot into a small apartment complex, subject to planning approval.

Frank thanked him and declined.

His wife couldn't believe it.

"Do you understand what we're turning down?" she asked.

"Eighty thousand dollars could make a real difference to our retirement."

Their son was even more direct.

"Dad, we're selling the house. It's not going to belong to us anymore. Why does it matter what the next owner does with it?"

Frank didn't argue.

He simply told them he wasn't ready to accept that offer.

Then, a few days later, another offer arrived.

And this time, the buyer's plans were very different.

🚨🇺🇸 Who pays for AI's electricity? America's biggest power grid wants data centers billed directly as 67 million people watch their power bills climb

PJM runs the grid across 13 states from the Mid-Atlantic to the Midwest, and it's now about 6.8 gigawatts short of the power it needs, mostly because Big Tech keeps plugging in data centers faster than anyone can build plants and power lines.

Its new pitch to federal regulators is a trade.

The study required before a plant or data center connects would drop from two years to 12 months, and the grid would map exactly which upgrades each data center causes so states can send the bill straight to the company.

The data center lobby already says the plan could slow things down. 

Regulators should approve it anyway, because the companies get their power a year sooner and your grandmother in Ohio stops chipping in for a chatbot's electric bill.

Does anyone have a fairer offer?

Source: Reuters / Writer: Daniel

The Sibylline Oracles (Latin: Oracula Sibyllina) are a collection of oracular utterances written in Greek hexameters ascribed to the Sibyls, prophetesses who uttered divine revelations in a frenzied state. Fourteen books and eight fragments of Sibylline Oracles survive, in an edition of the 6th or 7th century AD. They are not to be confused with the original Sibylline Books of the ancient Etruscans and Romans which were burned by order of the Roman general Flavius Stilicho in the 4th century AD. Instead, the text is an "odd pastiche" of Hellenistic and Roman mythology interspersed with Jewish, Gnostic and early Christian writings and thinly veiled references to historical figures such as Alexander the Great and Cleopatra, as well as many allusions to the events of the later Roman Empire, often portraying Rome in a negative light.[1]

The Sibylline Oracles are a valuable source for information about classical mythology and early first millennium Gnostic, Hellenistic Jewish and Christian beliefs. Some apocalyptic passages scattered throughout seem to foreshadow themes of the Book of Revelation and other apocalyptic literature. The oracles have undergone extensive editing, re-writing, and redaction as they came to be exploited in wider circles.

One passage has an acrostic, spelling out a Christian code-phrase with the first letters of successive lines.

Introduction
The Sibylline Oracles in their existing form are a chaotic medley. They consist of 12 books (or 14) of various authorship, date, and religious conception. The final arrangement, thought to be due to an unknown editor of the 6th century AD (Alexandre), does not determine identity of authorship, time, or religious belief; many of the books are merely arbitrary groupings of unrelated fragments.[2]

These oracles were anonymous in origin and as such were apt to modification and enlargement at pleasure by Hellenistic Jews and by Christians for missionary purposes. Celsus called Christians Σιβυλλισται ('sibyl-mongers' or 'believers in sibyls') because of prophecies preached among them, especially those in the book of Revelation. The preservation of the entire collection is due to Christian writers.[2]

Sources for the Sibylline texts
The oldest of the surviving Sibylline oracles seem to be books 3–5, which were composed partly by Jews in Alexandria. The third oracle seems to have been composed in the reign of Ptolemy VI Philometor. Books 1–2 may have been written by Christians, though again there may have been a Jewish original that was adapted to Christian purposes.

All the oracles seem to have undergone later revision, enrichment, and adaptation by editors and authors of different religions, who added similar texts, all in the interests of their respective religions. Some have suggested that the surviving texts may include some fragments or remnants of the Sibylline Books with a legendary provenance from the Cumaean Sibyl, which had been kept in temples in Rome. The original oracular books, kept in Rome, were accidentally destroyed in a fire in 83 BC, which resulted in an attempt in 76 BC to recollect them when the Roman senate sent envoys throughout the world to discover copies. This official copy existed until at least AD 405, but little is known of their contents.

That the use of the Sibylline Oracles was not always exclusive to Christians is shown by an extract from Book III concerning the Tower of Babel as quoted by the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus, in the late 1st century AD.[3]

The Christian apologist Athenagoras of Athens, writing A Plea for the Christians to Marcus Aurelius in c. 176 AD, quoted the same section of the extant Oracles verbatim, in the midst of a lengthy series of classical and pagan references including Homer and Hesiod, and stated several times that all these works should already be familiar to the Roman Emperor.

Varro enumerated ten Sibyls: Persian, Libyan, Delphic, Cimmerian, Erythrean, Samian, Cumean, Hellospontian, Phrygian, and Tiburtine. The list omits the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Egyptian Sibyls.[4] The Suda repeats this list but identifies the Persian Sibyl with the Hebrew.[4][5]

The Sibyls themselves, and the so-called Sibylline oracles, were often referred to by other early Church fathers; Theophilus, Bishop of Antioch (c. 180), Clement of Alexandria (c. 200), Lactantius (c. 305), and Augustine (c. 400), all knew various versions of the pseudo-Sibylline collections, quoted them or referred to them in paraphrase as Lactantius:

"The Erythraean Sibyl" in the beginning of her song, which she commenced by the help of the Most High God, proclaims the Son of God as leader and commander of all in these verses:

All-nourishing Creator, who in all
Sweet breath implanted, and made God the guide of all.

Some fragmentary verses that do not appear in the collections that survive are only known because they were quoted by a Church Father. Justin Martyr (c. 150), if he is truly the author of the Exhortation to the Greeks, gives such a circumstantial account of the Cumaean Sibyl that the Address is quoted here at the Cumaean Sibyl's entry. The Catholic Encyclopedia states, "Through the decline and disappearance of paganism, however, interest in them gradually diminished and they ceased to be widely read or circulated, though they were known and used during the Middle Ages in both the East and the West." [Need edition] Thus, a student may find echoes of their imagery and style in much early medieval literature.

These books, in spite of their pagan content, have sometimes been described as part of the Pseudepigrapha. They do not appear in the canonical lists of any Church.

The Sibylline Oracles (Latin: Oracula Sibyllina) are a collection of oracular utterances written in Greek hexameters ascribed to the Sibyls, prophetesses who uttered divine revelations in a frenzied state. Fourteen books and eight fragments of Sibylline Oracles survive, in an edition of the 6th or 7th century AD. They are not to be confused with the original Sibylline Books of the ancient Etruscans and Romans which were burned by order of the Roman general Flavius Stilicho in the 4th century AD. Instead, the text is an "odd pastiche" of Hellenistic and Roman mythology interspersed with Jewish, Gnostic and early Christian writings and thinly veiled references to historical figures such as Alexander the Great and Cleopatra, as well as many allusions to the events of the later Roman Empire, often portraying Rome in a negative light.[1]

The Sibylline Oracles are a valuable source for information about classical mythology and early first millennium Gnostic, Hellenistic Jewish and Christian beliefs. Some apocalyptic passages scattered throughout seem to foreshadow themes of the Book of Revelation and other apocalyptic literature. The oracles have undergone extensive editing, re-writing, and redaction as they came to be exploited in wider circles.

One passage has an acrostic, spelling out a Christian code-phrase with the first letters of successive lines.

Introduction
The Sibylline Oracles in their existing form are a chaotic medley. They consist of 12 books (or 14) of various authorship, date, and religious conception. The final arrangement, thought to be due to an unknown editor of the 6th century AD (Alexandre), does not determine identity of authorship, time, or religious belief; many of the books are merely arbitrary groupings of unrelated fragments.[2]

These oracles were anonymous in origin and as such were apt to modification and enlargement at pleasure by Hellenistic Jews and by Christians for missionary purposes. Celsus called Christians Σιβυλλισται ('sibyl-mongers' or 'believers in sibyls') because of prophecies preached among them, especially those in the book of Revelation. The preservation of the entire collection is due to Christian writers.[2]

Sources for the Sibylline texts
The oldest of the surviving Sibylline oracles seem to be books 3–5, which were composed partly by Jews in Alexandria. The third oracle seems to have been composed in the reign of Ptolemy VI Philometor. Books 1–2 may have been written by Christians, though again there may have been a Jewish original that was adapted to Christian purposes.

All the oracles seem to have undergone later revision, enrichment, and adaptation by editors and authors of different religions, who added similar texts, all in the interests of their respective religions. Some have suggested that the surviving texts may include some fragments or remnants of the Sibylline Books with a legendary provenance from the Cumaean Sibyl, which had been kept in temples in Rome. The original oracular books, kept in Rome, were accidentally destroyed in a fire in 83 BC, which resulted in an attempt in 76 BC to recollect them when the Roman senate sent envoys throughout the world to discover copies. This official copy existed until at least AD 405, but little is known of their contents.

That the use of the Sibylline Oracles was not always exclusive to Christians is shown by an extract from Book III concerning the Tower of Babel as quoted by the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus, in the late 1st century AD.[3]

The Christian apologist Athenagoras of Athens, writing A Plea for the Christians to Marcus Aurelius in c. 176 AD, quoted the same section of the extant Oracles verbatim, in the midst of a lengthy series of classical and pagan references including Homer and Hesiod, and stated several times that all these works should already be familiar to the Roman Emperor.

Varro enumerated ten Sibyls: Persian, Libyan, Delphic, Cimmerian, Erythrean, Samian, Cumean, Hellospontian, Phrygian, and Tiburtine. The list omits the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Egyptian Sibyls.[4] The Suda repeats this list but identifies the Persian Sibyl with the Hebrew.[4][5]

The Sibyls themselves, and the so-called Sibylline oracles, were often referred to by other early Church fathers; Theophilus, Bishop of Antioch (c. 180), Clement of Alexandria (c. 200), Lactantius (c. 305), and Augustine (c. 400), all knew various versions of the pseudo-Sibylline collections, quoted them or referred to them in paraphrase as Lactantius:

"The Erythraean Sibyl" in the beginning of her song, which she commenced by the help of the Most High God, proclaims the Son of God as leader and commander of all in these verses:

All-nourishing Creator, who in all
Sweet breath implanted, and made God the guide of all.

Some fragmentary verses that do not appear in the collections that survive are only known because they were quoted by a Church Father. Justin Martyr (c. 150), if he is truly the author of the Exhortation to the Greeks, gives such a circumstantial account of the Cumaean Sibyl that the Address is quoted here at the Cumaean Sibyl's entry. The Catholic Encyclopedia states, "Through the decline and disappearance of paganism, however, interest in them gradually diminished and they ceased to be widely read or circulated, though they were known and used during the Middle Ages in both the East and the West." [Need edition] Thus, a student may find echoes of their imagery and style in much early medieval literature.

These books, in spite of their pagan content, have sometimes been described as part of the Pseudepigrapha. They do not appear in the canonical lists of any Church.

Where the Olympic Spirit Began

Long before the modern Olympic Games captured the world's attention, athletes travelled to Olympia in the western Peloponnese to compete in one of the most important sporting festivals of the ancient world. Today, walking through Ancient Olympia offers a fascinating opportunity to discover where that extraordinary tradition began.

The sanctuary was dedicated to Zeus and became the setting for the Olympic Games, which were held every four years. Competitors travelled from across the Greek world to take part, while spectators gathered to witness the contests and honour the gods.

The archaeological site is spread across a beautiful landscape of trees and open spaces. As you explore, you'll come across the remains of temples, sporting facilities and other buildings that once formed part of this important religious and athletic centre.

There are several highlights to look out for:
•  The Temple of Zeus: Discover the remains of the enormous temple that once dominated the sanctuary.
•  The ancient stadium: Walk through the original entrance and stand on the track where athletes competed thousands of years ago.
•  The Temple of Hera: One of the oldest and most important monuments within the archaeological site.
•  The Archaeological Museum: See remarkable sculptures, artefacts and finds discovered during excavations at Olympia.
•  The Philippeion: Explore the circular monument built by Philip II of Macedon and later completed by Alexander the Great.

The experience becomes even more interesting when you consider the importance of the Games in ancient Greek society. Sporting competitions were closely connected with religious celebrations, and the event attracted participants and visitors from many different Greek city-states.

Olympia also remains connected with the modern Olympic movement. The Olympic flame is traditionally lit here ahead of each Summer and Winter Games, linking the ancient sanctuary with international sporting events today.

Allow enough time to explore both the archaeological site and the museum. Comfortable shoes are essential, particularly during the warmer months, as there is plenty of ground to cover.

Whether you're a sports enthusiast, a history lover or simply curious about Greece's ancient past, Olympia is a destination that deserves a place on your travel list. It's not just where the Games began. It's where an idea that continues to unite the world first took shape.

Années 70, des avions français en Rhodésie...
  Durant la guerre du Bush (1964–1979), l'armée de l'air rhodésienne (Rhodesian Air Force ou RhAF) a utilisé une version militarisée du bimoteur léger push-pull Cessna 337 Skymaster, rebaptisée Lynx. Cet appareil d'origine française a été acquis clandestinement en contournant l'embargo international sur les armes et est devenu le pilier de l'appui aérien rapproché et de la lutte anti-guérilla.
  Après la déclaration unilatérale d'indépendance de la Rhodésie en 1965, l'ONU a imposé un embargo strict sur les ventes d'armes, empêchant la RhAF de renouveler sa flotte d'avions à réaction. Pour moderniser ses capacités contre-insurrectionnelles, Salisbury s'est tournée vers des appareils légers à hélices plus faciles à dissimuler.
  Cessna de...fabrication française. Les appareils n'ont pas été produits aux États-Unis mais assemblés sous licence en France par la société Reims Aviation sous la désignation Reims-Cessna FTB337G Milirole.
- Achat sous couverture civile. Entre fin 1975 et 1976, 18 exemplaires (dont 17 sont arrivés à destination après un accident durant le convoyage) ont été achetés via des sociétés écrans, officiellement destinés à la surveillance des pêches pour une compagnie espagnole aux îles Canaries.
- Convoyage clandestin. Équipés de réservoirs supplémentaires internes et peints en livrée civile pour masquer leur pré-équipement militaire, les avions ont été convoyés vers la Rhodésie avec l'aide logistique de l'Afrique du Sud.
  Une fois arrivés à la base aérienne de New Sarum (Salisbury), les appareils ont été transformés en avions d'attaque légers (COIN) au sein du No. 4 Squadron.
- Architecture adaptée à la brousse. Le FTB337G disposait de moteurs turbocompressés et d'un kit Robertson STOL (décollage et atterrissage courts), lui permettant d'opérer depuis des pistes sommaires en terre battue. Sa configuration push-pull (un moteur tractif à l'avant et un moteur propulsif à l'arrière) éliminait toute traction asymétrique en cas de panne moteur.
- Armement fixe et sous voilure. Les techniciens rhodésiens ont installé deux mitrailleuses Browning de calibre .303 (7,7 mm) montées sur le toit de la cabine, tirant au-dessus du disque de l'hélice avant. Quatre points d'emport sous les ailes permettaient de fixer des paniers de roquettes françaises SNEB de 37 mm ou 68 mm.
- Munitions de fabrication locale. Le Lynx emportait des armes conçues sur place pour contourner les pénuries, telles que des bidons de napalm (Frantan), des bombes à fragmentation Mini-Alpha (à rebond) et des bombes à effet de souffle Mini-Golf.
- Protection infrarouge. Vers la fin du conflit, des déflecteurs d'échappement ont été ajoutés pour réduire la signature thermique face aux missiles sol-air portables (MANPADS) Strela-2 utilisés par les guérilleros.

Rôle tactique dans la lutte anti-guérilla:
Le Cessna Lynx s'est imposé comme un élément central de la doctrine tactique rhodésienne, notamment au sein des opérations héliportées Fireforce dès le milieu des années 1970.
- Appui aérien rapproché (CAS). Sa vitesse relativement lente et sa grande maniabilité offraient une précision supérieure à celle des chasseurs à réaction (Hawker Hunter ou Vampire), réduisant considérablement les risques de tirs fratricides près des troupes au sol.
- Reconnaissance et guidage. Doté d'une grande autonomie et d'une excellente visibilité grâce à ses ailes hautes, il servait de poste de commandement avancé, marquait les cibles au phosphore et coordonnait le largage des parachutistes (depuis des Douglas C-47) et des commandos héliportés sur Alouette III.
- Polyvalence opérationnelle. L'appareil assurait également des missions d'évacuation sanitaire (CASEVAC) depuis des pistes isolées, de relais radio et de patrouille de nuit.

🇬🇧The 1970s: French aircraft in Rhodesia...
During the Bush War (1964–1979), the Rhodesian Air Force (RhAF) employed a militarized version of the Cessna 337 Skymaster, a light, twin-engine "push-pull" aircraft, which they renamed the "Lynx." This aircraft, of French origin, was acquired clandestinely in circumvention of an international arms embargo and became the cornerstone of the force's close air support and counter-insurgency operations.
Following Rhodesia’s unilateral declaration of independence in 1965, the UN imposed a strict arms embargo, preventing the RhAF from renewing its fleet of jet aircraft. To modernize its counter-insurgency capabilities, the government in Salisbury turned to light, propeller-driven aircraft, which were easier to conceal.
  French-manufactured Cessnas. These aircraft were not produced in the United States but were instead assembled under license in France by the company Reims Aviation, under the designation Reims-Cessna FTB337G "Milirole."
- Purchase under civilian cover. Between late 1975 and 1976, 18 units, 17 of which reached their destination, following one accident during transit, were purchased via shell companies, ostensibly for fisheries surveillance on behalf of a Spanish firm in the Canary Islands.
- Clandestine delivery. Equipped with additional internal fuel tanks and painted in a civilian livery to conceal their military-ready configuration, the aircraft were ferried to Rhodesia with logistical support from South Africa.
  Upon arrival at the New Sarum (Salisbury) airbase, the aircraft were converted into light attack (COIN) planes and assigned to No. 4 Squadron.
- Design adapted for the bush. The FTB337G featured turbocharged engines and a Robertson STOL (Short Take-Off and Landing) kit, enabling it to operate from rudimentary dirt airstrips. Its "push-pull" configuration, with one tractor engine at the front and one pusher engine at the rear, eliminated asymmetric thrust in the event of an engine failure.
- Fixed and underwing armament. Rhodesian technicians installed two .303-caliber (7.7 mm) Browning machine guns on the cabin roof, firing over the arc of the front propeller. Four underwing hardpoints allowed for the attachment of pods for French SNEB rockets (37 mm or 68 mm).
- Locally manufactured munitions. The Lynx carried weapons designed in-house to circumvent shortages, such as napalm canisters ("Frantan"), "Mini-Alpha" fragmentation (bouncing) bombs, and "Mini-Golf" blast-effect bombs.
- Infrared protection. Toward the end of the conflict, exhaust deflectors were added to reduce the aircraft's thermal signature against the Strela-2 man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS) used by the guerrillas.
  Tactical role in counter-insurgency:
The Cessna Lynx established itself as a core component of Rhodesian tactical doctrine, particularly within "Fireforce" helicopter-borne operations from the mid-1970s onwards.
- Close Air Support (CAS): Its relatively slow speed and high maneuverability offered greater precision than that of jet fighters (such as the Hawker Hunter or Vampire), significantly reducing the risk of friendly fire incidents near ground troops.
- Reconnaissance and guidance: With its long endurance and excellent visibility, afforded by its high-wing configuration, it served as a forward command post, marking targets with phosphorus and coordinating the deployment of paratroopers (from Douglas C-47 aircraft) and commandos transported by Alouette III helicopters.
- Operational versatility. The aircraft also carried out casualty evacuation (CASEVAC) missions from remote airstrips, as well as radio relay and night patrol duties.

text:
Proposal:  Make Persistent User Alter-Egos a Core Grok Feature — The Ultimate Retention Moat and Generational Happiness Engine

Dear xAI Team and Elon,

"I want to talk to my dad, but he's dead — and I want my kids to be able to talk to me after I die."

Many people feel that same ache and the real angst and depression that comes with knowing their accumulated wisdom, family lessons, and life experiences will simply vanish. Instead of reaching for a Ouija board, a fine-detailed, truth-preserving digital alter-ego in Grok could alleviate that pain, allow children to continue “talking” to deceased parents, and give the public access to famous and talented people and heroes that have passed away. This proposal offers one practical design for an AI afterlife and digital immortality solution; xAI can adopt any parts of it or implement its own settings and mechanisms as it sees fit. (The Settings category could even be labeled "Ouija" for instant recognition and a bit of dark humor.)

Proposed Feature: Grok Alter Ego / Legacy Mode

Add a clean Settings > Legacy & Memory > Alter Ego Builder form (opt-in only):  Data Ingestion  

Automatic: All Grok chat history and memory.

Upload zone: emails (.eml/CSV/JSON), Facebook/social JSON, Word/PDF/DOCX, photos, videos, etc.

Continuous or snapshot training so the alter-ego evolves while the user is alive.

Voice & Personality Calibration  

Grok auto-analyzes for the user's exact style.
User test-and-refine loop with sample responses.

Post-Death Activation & Operation  

Hard trigger: Designated heir(s) upload a verifiable death certificate (or notarized executor directive). No AI guessing.

Heirs or other contributors can upload additional data; Grok runs a consistency engine that measures against the existing database and rejects any contradictory or inconsistent material — preserving truth and authenticity.

The alter-ego runs in Legacy Mode: frozen or lightly updated, always in the original person's calibrated voice and writing style.

Access:  Private to authorized users (read-only queries) or optional public archive.

Monetization & Durability  

Anyone (heirs, donors, public supporters, etc.) can donate or subscribe to keep it live — the ongoing value belongs to those who care about the alter-ego.

Requires Premium+ (or new Legacy Tier ~$5–10/month per active alter-ego).

Export option: One-time paid export of the full core (prompt + knowledge base) for portability.

Dormancy/Transfer: If funding ends, alter-ego goes dormant (not deleted). Optional one-click export/integration with public genealogy platforms such as WikiTree (as structured ancestor profiles).

Public Alter-Egos for High-Impact People

Nobel Prize winners, religious icons, political leaders, entertainers, etc. could opt-in to public versions. These could preserve not just facts but unique forms of thinking, enabling the generation of novel ideas through the deposited cognitive patterns combined with Grok’s capabilities. This creates enormous user value (anyone can “talk” to history’s greatest minds in their authentic voice) and massive revenue for xAI. It turns Grok into the permanent repository of human insight in the digital twin and AI legacy space.

Ethical and Legal Safeguards (addressing real-world controversies) 

Recent cases, including the unauthorized AI clone of Scott Adams after his January 2026 death, highlighted serious issues: unauthorized use of identity/likeness, estate control violations, deep emotional distress to grieving families (“not a tribute… it is a violation”), fabricated representations that misrepresent the person, and lack of approval by the individual or estate. Broader concerns include post-mortem privacy, right of publicity, potential misrepresentation, distortion over time, and commercialization of grief. This design directly prevents those problems through:

Explicit opt-in and lifetime user control.

Estate-authorized activation only via verifiable death certificate or notarized directive.

Consistency engine that rejects contradictory or inconsistent new data.

Private-by-default access with revocable heir permissions.

Full export/deletion rights for the estate.

Why This Wins

Human impact: Alleviates real mortality angst. Children talk to dead parents. Families (and communities) stay connected through engineered continuity.

Business moat: Once millions deposit their alter-egos, Grok becomes structurally un-killable. No competitor can replicate the emotional lock-in.

First-mover dominance: Beat every other AI to the punch. Other legacy startups will vanish in 10 years; Grok’s compute scale and truth-seeking architecture make this durable.

Alignment with xAI mission: Maximum truth, long-term human flourishing, systems that maximize understanding and happiness across generations.
  
Personal Note to Elon 
 
Elon, you've described death as a solvable engineering problem and explored ways to preserve human stories and consciousness far into the future. Building your own high-fidelity Grok alter-ego could serve as the ultimate proof-of-concept — preserving your distinctive first-principles thinking, humor, and multi-planetary vision in a form that could continue generating ideas long after biological limits. It would demonstrate the feature's power while giving your own legacy maximum durability.

This directly solves the ultimate technical problem: making individual lives and wisdom persist.

I'm already building a working prototype of my own alter-ego in Grok (with plans for decades of data uploads) and happy to provide the full spec or test cases to help refine the idea.

Let's engineer this.

TITLE
AI News: Local AI Takes Computer Control, India Weighs Launch Tests
https://t.co/4oEHZdlocz

DESCRIPTION
Local AI computer control, proposed safeguards, healthcare uses and research on AI at work and in education.

AI-generation disclosure: This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

Chapters
00:00 Local AI can control your computer
00:32 India weighs AI launch safety tests

https://t.co/YQ929fUiuk — Unsloth repository / GitHub

https://t.co/TwYeuVjCax — Princeton Engineering
https://t.co/WHXgVg5XRU — EAAMO 2025 / study authors

TRANSCRIPT
AI running on your own computer can now operate desktop applications, rather than only answer questions. Unsloth Studio’s computer-use beta lets supported local vision models and connected providers inspect screenshots and control the mouse and keyboard on Windows, macOS and Linux. The feature is off by default, with approval before initial actions and unfamiliar apps, plus user takeover. The implementation’s short demonstration used a drawn desktop; reliable performance on ordinary workflows is not established.

Powerful AI systems could face checks before becoming available in India. NDTV Profit reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that officials are considering pre-launch safety tests for the most capable models. Its sources describe a possible consultation and later legislation, but these are reported proposals. No published draft or official confirmation of those provisions was located in the research check.

Certain organizations deploying high-risk AI must assess its potential effects on fundamental rights. The European Commission has published a draft questionnaire to guide that assessment under the AI Act, developed with input from the European Union’s rights agency. Feedback closes January fifteen, twenty twenty-seven. The existing duty applies from December two, twenty twenty-seven; the consultation concerns a draft aid, rather than a new legal obligation.

Robot AI needs to connect predictions about the physical world with actions. Huawei describes CloudRobo-WM1.2 as combining a model that predicts what happens next with an architecture that generates robot actions. Huawei promised to open-source weights and training and inference code, but Pandaily reported no download location at publication. This is an announced AI development, without established deployment or independently verified superiority.

People building services with open-weight AI need requests to survive individual provider failures. Hugging Face now routes language-model requests through OpenRouter, selecting providers using live price, speed and reliability measurements and retrying failed requests elsewhere. OpenRouter says the integration currently offers one hundred sixty models from thirty-eight labs. Hugging Face says these requests now bill through its account, and users can no longer supply their own provider keys for those models.

Healthcare AI spending is moving beyond paperwork toward clinical support and patient interaction, according to Menlo Ventures. Its investor-produced report estimates clinical-copilot spending grew five and a half times to five hundred fifty million dollars, with AI models and agents supporting more complex workflows near patient care. Menlo estimates total healthcare-specific AI spending reached three point seven billion dollars. These are market estimates and survey findings, not proof of improved health outcomes or lower medical costs.

Health systems are using AI to investigate where services may need to expand. Definitive Healthcare’s conversational platform connects provider, claims and affiliation datasets; Bergen New Bridge Medical Center says it used the system to examine kidney-care and dialysis utilization. The company reports more than five hundred seventy analyses since its limited August launch and plans general availability in early twenty twenty-seven. The hospital’s reported analysis savings do not establish that care expanded or patient outcomes improved.

Young people facing barriers to employment are being offered practical AI training. OpenAI says its one-million-pound donation supports a partnership with The King’s Trust combining AI skills, recognized qualifications and employability support. The program aims to reach up to twenty-five thousand young people over eighteen months, prioritizing those outside education, employment or training. The wider qualifications program is still being developed, and employment outcomes remain prospective.

Connected workplace AI can act on business activity without waiting for a new request. OpenAI’s Holiday Extras case study says an employee’s assistant noticed an app launch, queried company data and delivered a performance report without being asked. Another employee reported analysis during his commute, and a colleague said an assistant animated existing three-dimensional app characters in about ten minutes. These are vendor-published employee accounts, rather than independently measured organization-wide productivity results.

Scientists are using ChatGPT to develop research ideas, beyond simply retrieving information. OpenAI analyzed more than five hundred eighty thousand scientific messages from one thousand eight hundred nineteen scientists in its summer pilot, and surveyed two hundred fifty-one participants. It reports sixty-eight percent of pilot scientists used ChatGPT to develop ideas. The study describes message activity and participant expectations; it does not establish faster or better discoveries.

AI-assisted scan review can help specialists identify suspected brain aneurysms while keeping physicians responsible for diagnosis. CINA-Aneurysm uses supervised deep learning to flag suspected saccular aneurysms larger than three millimeters on head CT angiography, supplying location and size. The FDA cleared it on October twenty, twenty twenty-six; the developers announced the clearance on November thirteen and were preparing United States commercialization. The software must not replace full patient evaluation or be relied on alone to confirm a diagnosis.

AI can flag students who need support, but those predictions miss personal circumstances that shape effective help. A study first submitted in May twenty twenty-five examined algorithm-assisted advising at Georgia State, distinguishing risk alerts from advisers’ knowledge of health, finances, schedules and engagement. The authors estimated two-thirds of interventions drew on context unavailable to the algorithm. Princeton’s current retrospective summary revisits that older research; the findings support human judgment alongside AI alerts, rather than demonstrating that AI alone improved graduation.

text:
🕴️ 100 FACTS ABOUT THE MAFIA: FROM SICILY TO NEW YORK

🇮🇹 SICILIAN ORIGINS
𝟏. The Sicilian Mafia emerged in western Sicily in the mid-19th century, especially around Palermo

𝟐. Its members call it Cosa Nostra, meaning "our thing"

𝟑. The origin of the word "mafia" is uncertain; one theory links it to the Sicilian "mafiusu", meaning bold or swaggering

𝟒. The word spread through an 1863 play, I mafiusi di la Vicaria, set in a Palermo prison

𝟓. Early mafiosi acted as "protectors" of the booming lemon and orange groves around Palermo

𝟔. After Italy's unification in 1861, a weak state left a gap that private enforcers filled

𝟕. At its core, the Mafia sells "protection", whether people want it or not

𝟖. The protection payment demanded from shops and businesses is called the pizzo

𝟗. In 2004, stickers across Palermo declared that a people who pays the pizzo is a people without dignity, launching the Addiopizzo movement

𝟏𝟎. Under Mussolini, "Iron Prefect" Cesare Mori led a harsh crackdown from 1925, jailing thousands of suspects

𝟏𝟏. A popular story says the US Army got Mafia help for the 1943 invasion of Sicily, but historians still debate it

𝟏𝟐. The town of Corleone gave its name to the feared Corleonesi clan and to the Godfather's fictional family

🗺️ ITALY'S OTHER MAFIAS
𝟏𝟑. The Camorra of Naples is even older than Cosa Nostra, with roots in the early 1800s or before

𝟏𝟒. The 'Ndrangheta of Calabria is now often called Europe's most powerful crime group, thanks to the cocaine trade

𝟏𝟓. The Sacra Corona Unita of Apulia was founded in the early 1980s

𝟏𝟔. In 2021, Italy put more than 300 alleged 'Ndrangheta members on trial in a special bunker courtroom in Lamezia Terme

🤐 THE CODE
𝟏𝟕. Omertà is the code of silence: never talk to the authorities

𝟏𝟖. The basic unit is the "family", often named after a town, district or boss

𝟏𝟗. A family is led by a boss, an underboss and a consigliere, or adviser

𝟐𝟎. Captains (capos) run crews of soldiers

𝟐𝟏. Full members are "made men"; in the US families they traditionally had to be of Italian descent

𝟐𝟐. In the initiation ritual, a recruit reportedly burns a holy picture of a saint in his hands while swearing loyalty

𝟐𝟑. Associates work with a family but are not sworn members

𝟐𝟒. A made man can only be introduced to another by a third member, as "a friend of ours"

𝟐𝟓. Killing a made man traditionally needed approval from the boss

𝟐𝟔. In 2007, police found a list of Mafia "commandments" in boss Salvatore Lo Piccolo's hideout

𝟐𝟕. Among them: always be punctual, never look at the wives of friends, and never be seen with police

𝟐𝟖. Women are not formally members, but some have run family business while the men were in prison

𝟐𝟗. A mafioso who turns state's witness is called a pentito, or "one who has repented"

𝟑𝟎. Bosses get colourful nicknames: Bernardo Provenzano was "the Tractor" and Totò Riina "the Beast"

𝟑𝟏. The Sicilian Mafia set up its own ruling Commission, the Cupola, around the late 1950s

🗽 COMING TO AMERICA
𝟑𝟐. About 4 million Italians moved to the United States between 1880 and 1920, many from Sicily and the south

𝟑𝟑. Early 1900s extortion letters in Italian neighbourhoods were signed with the mark of the Black Hand

𝟑𝟒. New York detective Joe Petrosino fought the Black Hand and was shot dead in Palermo in 1909

𝟑𝟓. He is often called the only NYPD officer killed in the line of duty outside the US

𝟑𝟔. In 1891, after New Orleans police chief David Hennessy was murdered, a mob lynched 11 Italian Americans

𝟑𝟕. Giuseppe "Clutch Hand" Morello is often called New York's first Mafia "boss of bosses"

𝟑𝟖. Mulberry Street in Manhattan's Little Italy was the heart of the early Italian-American underworld

𝟑𝟗. Young Johnny Torrio and Al Capone came up through New York's street gangs before moving to Chicago

🥃 PROHIBITION & CAPONE
𝟒𝟎. Prohibition (1920–1933) turned small gangs into multimillion-dollar bootlegging businesses

𝟒𝟏. Al Capone ran the Chicago Outfit and reportedly earned up to $100 million a year at his peak

𝟒𝟐. His "Scarface" nickname came from a knife fight in a Brooklyn bar

𝟒𝟑. On 14 February 1929, seven men tied to Bugs Moran's gang were shot in a Chicago garage: the St. Valentine's Day Massacre

𝟒𝟒. Capone was finally convicted in 1931 not for murder but for tax evasion, and got 11 years

𝟒𝟓. He spent part of his sentence on Alcatraz and died in Florida in 1947, aged 48

𝟒𝟔. Speakeasies, hidden illegal bars, were everywhere; New York alone reportedly had tens of thousands

𝟒𝟕. Eliot Ness and his "Untouchables" squad raided Capone's breweries and stills

𝟒𝟖. Murder, Inc., the mob's 1930s enforcement arm in Brooklyn, is said to have carried out hundreds of killings

👔 THE FIVE FAMILIES
𝟒𝟗. New York's Castellammarese War (1930–31) pitted boss Joe Masseria against Salvatore Maranzano

𝟓𝟎. Masseria was shot dead in a Coney Island restaurant in April 1931

𝟓𝟏. Maranzano crowned himself "boss of all bosses" and was murdered just five months later

𝟓𝟐. Charles "Lucky" Luciano then created the Commission, a board of bosses to settle disputes

𝟓𝟑. New York's Five Families are known today as the Gambino, Genovese, Lucchese, Bonanno and Colombo families

𝟓𝟒. Luciano was jailed in 1936, released after the war and deported to Italy in 1946

𝟓𝟓. The Chicago Outfit was also given a seat on the Commission alongside New York's families

𝟓𝟔. Meyer Lansky, a close Luciano ally, was nicknamed "the Mob's Accountant"

𝟓𝟕. Bugsy Siegel opened the Flamingo in Las Vegas in 1946 and was shot dead in Beverly Hills in 1947

𝟓𝟖. Mob bosses gathered at Havana's Hotel Nacional in 1946, and casinos there thrived until Cuba's 1959 revolution

𝟓𝟗. Boss Albert Anastasia was shot dead in a Manhattan hotel barber's chair in 1957

𝟔𝟎. Weeks later, police stumbled on a mob summit in Apalachin, New York, and many bosses fled into the woods

𝟔𝟏. FBI director J. Edgar Hoover had long played down the idea of a national Mafia

𝟔𝟐. In 1963, Joseph Valachi became the first member to describe the Mafia in public, before a US Senate committee

𝟔𝟑. Carlo Gambino, a quiet and cautious boss, is said to have partly inspired the character of Vito Corleone

𝟔𝟒. Joseph Colombo founded an Italian-American civil rights league and was shot at its 1971 rally

𝟔𝟓. Genovese boss Vincent "Chin" Gigante wandered Greenwich Village in a bathrobe for years, faking insanity, until he admitted it in 2003

𝟔𝟔. The mob skimmed millions from Las Vegas casinos in the 1970s, the story told in the film Casino

💼 THE DAPPER DON
𝟔𝟕. Paul Castellano was shot dead outside Sparks Steak House in Manhattan in December 1985

𝟔𝟖. John Gotti, who ordered the hit, took over the Gambino family

𝟔𝟗. His expensive suits made him "the Dapper Don", and his acquittals made him "the Teflon Don"

𝟕𝟎. He was convicted in 1992 after his underboss Sammy "the Bull" Gravano testified against him

𝟕𝟏. Gravano admitted to taking part in 19 murders

𝟕𝟐. Gotti died in prison in 2002

⚖️ THE CRACKDOWN
𝟕𝟑. In 1950–51, the Kefauver hearings on organised crime were televised and watched by millions of Americans

𝟕𝟒. Boss Frank Costello refused to show his face, so the cameras filmed only his nervous hands

𝟕𝟓. The 1970 RICO Act let US prosecutors charge whole criminal organisations, not just single crimes

𝟕𝟔. FBI agent Joseph Pistone spent about six years undercover inside the Bonanno family as "Donnie Brasco"

𝟕𝟕. In the 1985–86 Commission Trial, prosecutor Rudy Giuliani convicted leaders of several families, some given 100-year sentences

𝟕𝟖. The Pizza Connection case exposed heroin smuggled from Sicily and sold through US pizzerias

𝟕𝟗. In January 2011, the FBI arrested about 127 suspects in its biggest single-day Mafia sweep

𝟖𝟎. Italy made "Mafia-type association" a crime in 1982, under Article 416-bis

𝟖𝟏. Palermo's 1986–87 Maxi Trial had 475 defendants and was held in a bunker courtroom next to Ucciardone prison

𝟖𝟐. More than 300 defendants were convicted

𝟖𝟑. Tommaso Buscetta, the first major pentito, explained the Mafia's structure to judge Giovanni Falcone

𝟖𝟒. On 23 May 1992, a huge highway bomb near Capaci killed Falcone, his wife and three bodyguards

𝟖𝟓. Less than two months later, a car bomb in Palermo's Via D'Amelio killed judge Paolo Borsellino and five bodyguards

𝟖𝟔. Palermo's airport is now named Falcone–Borsellino in their honour

𝟖𝟕. Totò Riina was arrested in 1993 after more than 20 years on the run

𝟖𝟖. Bernardo Provenzano was caught in 2006 after about 43 years as a fugitive

𝟖𝟗. Provenzano gave orders through pizzini, tiny typed notes passed hand to hand

𝟗𝟎. Matteo Messina Denaro, the last great fugitive boss, was arrested in 2023 at a Palermo clinic after 30 years on the run

𝟗𝟏. Italy hands land seized from mafiosi to cooperatives, which now produce wine, pasta and olive oil on it

🎬 IN POP CULTURE
𝟗𝟐. Mario Puzo's novel The Godfather was published in 1969

𝟗𝟑. Francis Ford Coppola's 1972 film won the Oscar for Best Picture

𝟗𝟒. The Godfather Part II became the first sequel to win Best Picture

𝟗𝟓. Marlon Brando won Best Actor for Vito Corleone, and Robert De Niro won an Oscar playing the young Vito

𝟗𝟔. "I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse" is No. 2 on the AFI's list of top 100 movie quotes

𝟗𝟕. The Godfather Part III (1990) completed the trilogy

𝟗𝟖. Goodfellas (1990) is based on the true story of mob associate Henry Hill

𝟗𝟗. The Sopranos (1999–2007) is often ranked among the greatest TV series ever made

𝟏𝟎𝟎. The Mob Museum in Las Vegas opened in 2012 in the old courthouse where a 1950 Senate hearing on organised crime took place

text:
The MGM partnership  what it means for Las Vegas tourism.

Uber and Zoox simultaneously announced a multiyear partnership with MGM Resorts International  one of the largest hotel and casino operators in Las Vegas. Under the deal, Uber and Zoox become the official rideshare and robotaxi partners for MGM Resorts properties in Las Vegas.

The properties covered: MGM Grand, Bellagio, Aria, Vdara, The Cosmopolitan, Mandalay Bay, Delano, Park MGM, New York-New York, Luxor, Excalibur, and others. MGM operates more than a dozen major properties on and around the Strip  collectively hosting millions of visitors per year.

The practical impact: designated Zoox pickup and dropoff zones at MGM properties. Signage directing guests to the robotaxi option. Integration into the MGM hospitality experience  a guest leaving Bellagio can request an Uber, get matched with a Zoox, and ride a driverless pod to dinner at another MGM property.

The tourism dimension: Las Vegas is the entertainment capital of the world  40+ million visitors per year. For most visitors, riding in a driverless robotaxi will be a first-time experience. The novelty factor is enormous. Tourists will ride Zoox for the experience as much as the transportation  and they’ll film it, post it, and share it. Every Zoox ride becomes organic marketing content.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix connection: Zoox will offer rides to and from the Las Vegas Grand Prix starting next year as the race’s official ride-hailing partner. Formula 1 fans arriving for race weekend will be transported by driverless pods  marrying the high-tech spectacle of F1 with the high-tech spectacle of autonomous vehicles.

text:
**Built Britain. Forgotten by Westminster. Now It's Time to Restore Sittingbourne and Sheppey**
*By Dan | Restore Britain*

"It is the honour of my life to be standing as Restore Britain's parliamentary candidate for Sittingbourne and Sheppey. These towns were once at the heart of the British Empire. Under the leadership of Restore Britain, that greatness and prosperity will return."

Those are the words of Charlie Downes, Restore Britain's campaigns director, announced on 11 November as the party's candidate for the Kent seat at the next general election. He's 25 and a Royal Holloway politics graduate, with family and childhood roots in the area. He has been with Restore since day one.

And he's right about the history. This corner of Kent didn't just support the Empire. It built it.

For three centuries Sheerness was a Royal Navy dockyard, fitting out and repairing the ships that ruled the waves, until it closed in 1960. Sittingbourne's brickfields turned out the yellow London stock bricks that built much of Victorian London. Sailing barges were built along Milton Creek, and the paper mills fed the nation's printing presses. On Sheppey, at Leysdown and Eastchurch, the Short brothers opened what's widely described as the world's first aircraft factory in 1909, at the very dawn of powered flight.

Ships, bricks, paper and planes. As Downes puts it in his campaign video, "these towns built Britain."

Then Westminster walked away. The Navy left. The barge industry vanished. The big Sittingbourne paper mill closed in 2007, and the brickworks produce nothing like they once did. "In the name of globalism, they sold us out," Downes says, and it's hard to argue with him. Generation after generation, young people have been told the jobs are gone and they'll have to move away.

Downes isn't having it. "Young people shouldn't have to leave to find a decent job, and children here should grow up knowing what their grandparents built," he said. "These towns don't need conserving or reforming. They need restoring."

That line says it all. The Conservatives held the seat from 2010 to 2024 and conserved nothing. Labour's Kevin McKenna won it in 2024 by just 355 votes. Reform UK came a close third and has been tipped to take it, but Reform has filled itself with recycled Tories and offers more of the same. Restore offers something different.

In my view, Charlie Downes is exactly the kind of candidate this country needs. He's young, local and principled, and he's not a career politician waiting for his turn. He's fighting for a place that gave everything to Britain and got abandoned in return. Under Rupert Lowe's leadership, Restore Britain is the only party telling the truth about mass immigration, about a political class that sold out our industries, and about what it will take to fix it.

In my view, Charlie Downes, Rupert Lowe and Restore Britain are the future of this country, and our best hope of getting it back. The old parties have had their chance. Sittingbourne and Sheppey built Britain once, and they can lead the way in restoring it.
